chapters.title: Before the first page

paras.en: The Myth of Sisyphus is a short philosophical essay by Albert Camus. He finished it in February 1941, when he was only twenty-seven, and it was published in Paris by Gallimard in October 1942, in the middle of the German occupation of France. The book asks one question and refuses to run away from it: if life has no meaning that we can prove, is it still worth living? Camus's answer, reached slowly and honestly, is yes — but a very particular kind of yes, one that keeps its eyes open.
paras.uz: «Sizif afsonasi» — Alber Kamyuning qisqa falsafiy essesi. U uni 1941-yil fevralida, endigina yigirma yetti yoshida tugatgan; kitob 1942-yil oktabrida, Fransiya nemislar ishg'oli ostida bo'lgan bir paytda, Parijda Gallimar nashriyotida chop etilgan. Kitob bitta savol beradi va undan qochmaydi: agar hayotning biz isbotlay oladigan ma'nosi bo'lmasa, u baribir yashashga arziydimi? Kamyuning sekin va halol erishgan javobi — ha; lekin bu ko'zlarini ochiq tutadigan, juda o'ziga xos «ha».

paras.en: Camus thought of his early work as a cycle of three forms that explore the same idea, which he called the absurd. The novel was The Stranger (1942), the play was Caligula (written in these years, staged in 1945), and the essay was The Myth of Sisyphus. The novel shows a man who lives the absurd without explaining it; the play shows an emperor who pushes the absurd to murder and madness; the essay tries to think the absurd through with logic. If you have read our study edition of The Stranger, you will meet Meursault's world again here — this time as an argument.
paras.uz: Kamyu o'zining ilk ijodini bir g'oyani — u «absurd» deb atagan narsani — uch xil shaklda o'rganadigan tsikl deb bilgan. Roman — «Begona» (1942), pyesa — «Kaligula» (shu yillarda yozilgan, 1945-yilda sahnalashtirilgan), esse esa — «Sizif afsonasi». Roman absurdni tushuntirmasdan yashaydigan odamni ko'rsatadi; pyesa absurdni qotillik va telbalikkacha olib boradigan imperatorni ko'rsatadi; esse esa absurdni mantiq bilan oxirigacha o'ylab chiqishga urinadi. Agar «Begona»ning o'quv nashrimizni o'qigan bo'lsangiz, bu yerda Merso dunyosini yana uchratasiz — bu safar dalil shaklida.

paras.en: The essay is dedicated to Pascal Pia, the journalist who gave young Camus his first newspaper job in Algiers. It opens with an epigraph from the ancient Greek poet Pindar, which says, in short: my soul, do not long for an immortal life, but use up everything that is possible. This line is the whole book in miniature. Camus will not ask for eternity, heaven or a hidden meaning. He will ask what a person can do inside the limits of one mortal life — and how far those limits can be pushed.
paras.uz: Esse Kamyuga Jazoirda birinchi gazeta ishini bergan jurnalist Paskal Piyaga bag'ishlangan. U qadimgi yunon shoiri Pindardan olingan epigraf bilan ochiladi; uning mazmuni qisqacha: ey ruhim, abadiy hayotni orzu qilma, balki mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsani oxirigacha sarfla. Bu satr — butun kitobning kichik nusxasi. Kamyu abadiyat, jannat yoki yashirin ma'no so'ramaydi. U bitta o'lar hayot chegaralari ichida inson nima qila olishini — va bu chegaralarni qanchalik kengaytirish mumkinligini so'raydi.

paras.en: Before the essay begins, Camus adds an important note. He says that the pages which follow deal with an absurd sensibility that can be found everywhere in his age — not with an absurd philosophy, which, in his view, his age had not really produced. In other words, he is not inventing a system. He is describing a feeling that many people in the twentieth century shared: the sense that the old answers — religion, progress, reason — no longer hold, and that nothing has replaced them.
paras.uz: Esse boshlanishidan oldin Kamyu muhim izoh qo'shadi. U keyingi sahifalar o'z davrida hamma joyda uchraydigan absurd sezgi haqida ekanini — absurd falsafa haqida emasligini aytadi, chunki uning fikricha, davri haqiqiy absurd falsafa yaratmagan edi. Boshqacha aytganda, u tizim ixtiro qilmayapti. U XX asrda ko'p odamlar baham ko'rgan tuyg'uni tasvirlayapti: eski javoblar — din, taraqqiyot, aql — endi tayanch bo'la olmasligi va ularning o'rnini hech narsa bosmagani tuyg'usini.

paras.en: Camus also says that he is describing, as honestly as possible, an intellectual illness, without mixing into it any metaphysics or belief. This is a promise of method. He will not start from what he hopes is true. He will start only from what he knows for certain, and he will refuse every conclusion that goes beyond it. Later in the book he calls this rule 'lucidity' — seeing clearly — and it is the most important virtue in the whole essay.
paras.uz: Kamyu shuningdek u intellektual kasallikni, unga hech qanday metafizika yoki e'tiqod aralashtirmasdan, iloji boricha halol tasvirlayotganini aytadi. Bu — usul haqidagi va'da. U haqiqat bo'lishini umid qilgan narsadan boshlamaydi. U faqat aniq bilgan narsasidan boshlaydi va undan oshib ketadigan har qanday xulosani rad etadi. Kitobning keyingi qismida u bu qoidani «ravshanlik» (lucidity) — aniq ko'rish — deb ataydi va bu butun essedagi eng muhim fazilatdir.

paras.en: The book has four main parts. The first, An Absurd Reasoning, defines the absurd and asks whether it leads to suicide. The second, The Absurd Man, gives portraits of people who live the absurd: the seducer Don Juan, the actor and the conqueror. The third, Absurd Creation, asks what art and the novel can be in an absurd world, and studies Dostoevsky. The fourth, very short, is The Myth of Sisyphus itself. Most editions also include an appendix on Franz Kafka, which German censorship removed from the first French edition because Kafka was Jewish.
paras.uz: Kitob to'rt asosiy qismdan iborat. Birinchisi — «Absurd mulohaza» — absurdni ta'riflaydi va u o'z joniga qasd qilishga olib boradimi, degan savolni beradi. Ikkinchisi — «Absurd inson» — absurdni yashaydigan odamlar portretlarini beradi: vasvasachi Don Juan, aktyor va istilochi. Uchinchisi — «Absurd ijod» — absurd dunyoda san'at va roman nima bo'la olishini so'raydi va Dostoyevskiyni tahlil qiladi. To'rtinchisi, juda qisqa qismi — «Sizif afsonasi»ning o'zi. Ko'pchilik nashrlarda Frans Kafka haqidagi ilova ham bor; nemis senzurasi uni birinchi fransuzcha nashrdan olib tashlagan edi, chunki Kafka yahudiy edi.

paras.en: The essay was written in hard years. Europe was at war, France had collapsed in a few weeks in 1940, and Camus himself was ill with tuberculosis, a disease that had already threatened his life when he was seventeen. He had lost his father in the First World War before he could remember him, and he grew up poor in Algiers with a nearly deaf mother who could not read. None of this is mentioned in the book, but it explains its tone: it is the thinking of someone who knows that death is near and real.
paras.uz: Esse og'ir yillarda yozilgan. Yevropada urush borardi, Fransiya 1940-yilda bir necha hafta ichida qulagan edi, Kamyuning o'zi esa o'n yetti yoshidayoq hayotiga xavf solgan sil kasalligi bilan og'rirdi. U otasini Birinchi jahon urushida — uni eslay oladigan yoshga yetmasidan — yo'qotgan va Jazoirda deyarli kar, o'qishni bilmaydigan onasi bilan qashshoqlikda o'sgan. Kitobda bularning hech biri tilga olinmaydi, lekin ular uning ohangini tushuntiradi: bu o'lim yaqin va haqiqiy ekanini biladigan odamning fikrlashi.

paras.en: It is also a book written by a lover of life. Camus grew up between the sea and the sun of North Africa, he swam, played football as a goalkeeper, loved the theatre and the company of friends. His first books, Betwixt and Between and Nuptials, are full of the body's happiness under the Mediterranean light. The Myth of Sisyphus must be read with both sides in mind: the cold clarity of a man who refuses comforting lies, and the warm hunger of a man who does not want to give up a single day.
paras.uz: Bu, shuningdek, hayotni sevgan odam yozgan kitob. Kamyu Shimoliy Afrikaning dengizi va quyoshi orasida o'sgan, suzgan, futbolda darvozabon bo'lib o'ynagan, teatrni va do'stlar davrasini sevgan. Uning ilk kitoblari — «Ters va o'ng» va «To'ylar» — O'rta yer dengizi nuri ostidagi tana baxtiga to'la. «Sizif afsonasi»ni ikkala tomonni yodda tutib o'qish kerak: tasalli beruvchi yolg'onlarni rad etgan odamning sovuq ravshanligi va birorta kunidan ham voz kechishni istamagan odamning iliq tashnaligi.

paras.en: A word about this edition. The Myth of Sisyphus is still protected by copyright, so WordDrop cannot print Camus's own sentences. What you will read is a full study edition written by WordDrop: every part, chapter and argument of the essay is explained in order, in clear English, with an Uzbek translation, vocabulary, questions and notes. The few famous phrases we quote are very short and always marked. Our aim is that, after this book, you can open the original and recognise every step of the road.
paras.uz: Bu nashr haqida bir so'z. «Sizif afsonasi» hali ham mualliflik huquqi bilan himoyalangan, shuning uchun WordDrop Kamyuning o'z jumlalarini chop eta olmaydi. Siz o'qiydigan matn — WordDrop yozgan to'liq o'quv nashri: essening har bir qismi, bobi va dalili tartib bilan, tushunarli ingliz tilida, o'zbekcha tarjimasi, lug'ati, savollari va izohlari bilan bayon qilingan. Biz keltiradigan bir necha mashhur iboralar juda qisqa va doim belgilangan. Maqsadimiz — bu kitobdan keyin asl matnni ochib, yo'lning har bir qadamini taniy olishingiz.

paras.en: One more warning before we start. The first chapter of the essay is about suicide, and Camus discusses it directly and calmly, as a philosophical question. His conclusion is a firm no: the whole essay is an argument against suicide and against despair. Still, if these questions touch you personally and painfully, it is good to talk to someone you trust, or to a doctor or counsellor. Philosophy can help us think, but nobody should carry such weight alone.
paras.uz: Boshlashdan oldin yana bir ogohlantirish. Essening birinchi bobi o'z joniga qasd qilish haqida va Kamyu uni falsafiy savol sifatida to'g'ridan-to'g'ri va xotirjam muhokama qiladi. Uning xulosasi qat'iy «yo'q»: butun esse o'z joniga qasd qilishga va umidsizlikka qarshi dalildir. Falsafa fikrlashga yordam beradi, lekin hech kim bunday og'irlikni yolg'iz ko'tarmasligi kerak.

chapters.title: Absurdity and suicide
chapters.title_uz: Absurd va o'z joniga qasd qilish

paras.en: The essay begins with one of the most famous opening lines in modern philosophy. Camus declares that there is only one truly serious philosophical problem, and it is suicide. To decide whether life is or is not worth living is, for him, to answer the basic question of philosophy. Everything else — whether the world has three dimensions, whether the mind has nine or twelve categories — comes afterwards. Those are games, he says; first one must answer.
paras.uz: Esse zamonaviy falsafadagi eng mashhur boshlanishlardan biri bilan ochiladi. Kamyu haqiqatan ham jiddiy bo'lgan yagona falsafiy muammo bor, u ham bo'lsa o'z joniga qasd qilish, deb e'lon qiladi. Uning uchun hayot yashashga arziydimi yoki yo'qmi, degan qarorga kelish falsafaning asosiy savoliga javob berish demakdir. Qolgan hamma narsa — dunyo uch o'lchovlimi, aqlning to'qqizta yoki o'n ikkita kategoriyasi bormi — keyin keladi. Bular o'yinlar, deydi u; avval javob berish kerak.

paras.en: How does he know which question is most urgent? By looking at what people are ready to die for, or what makes them die. He gives the example of Galileo, who held a scientific truth of great importance and yet gave it up very easily when his life was threatened by the Inquisition. In a sense, Camus says, Galileo was right: that truth was not worth burning for. Whether the earth goes round the sun or the sun round the earth is, at bottom, unimportant to a human life.
paras.uz: U qaysi savol eng shoshilinch ekanini qanday biladi? Odamlar nima uchun o'lishga tayyor ekaniga yoki ularni nima o'limga olib borishiga qarab. U Galiley misolini keltiradi: Galiley katta ahamiyatga ega ilmiy haqiqatni bilardi, lekin inkvizitsiya hayotiga tahdid qilganda undan juda oson voz kechdi. Kamyuning aytishicha, ma'lum ma'noda Galiley haq edi: bu haqiqat gulxanda yonishga arzimasdi. Yer Quyosh atrofida aylanadimi yoki Quyosh Yer atrofidami — inson hayoti uchun, aslini olganda, ahamiyatsiz.

paras.en: On the other hand, he notes, many people die because they judge that life is not worth living. And others, paradoxically, let themselves be killed for ideas or illusions that give them a reason for living — so that a reason for living is also an excellent reason for dying. The question of the meaning of life is therefore the most urgent of all questions, because the answer is not only thought; it is acted out with the body.
paras.uz: Boshqa tomondan, deydi u, ko'p odamlar hayot yashashga arzimaydi, degan xulosaga kelgani uchun o'ladi. Boshqalar esa, paradoksal tarzda, ularga yashash uchun sabab beradigan g'oyalar yoki xayollar uchun o'ldirilishga yo'l qo'yadi — demak, yashash uchun sabab ayni paytda o'lish uchun ham ajoyib sababdir. Shuning uchun hayot ma'nosi haqidagi savol barcha savollarning eng shoshilinchidir, chunki javob faqat o'ylanmaydi; u tana bilan amalga oshiriladi.

paras.en: Camus makes clear that he will not treat suicide as a social phenomenon, the way a sociologist would count cases, or as a matter of psychology and illness. He is interested in the relation between individual thought and suicide. An act like this, he says, is prepared in the silence of the heart, the way a great work of art is prepared, and the person himself often does not know it. One day the person acts. Newspapers then speak of private sorrows or incurable illness, which may be true, but the real beginning is hidden.
paras.uz: Kamyu o'z joniga qasd qilishni sotsiolog holatlarni sanagandek ijtimoiy hodisa sifatida yoki psixologiya va kasallik masalasi sifatida ko'rib chiqmasligini aniq aytadi. Uni shaxsiy fikr va o'z joniga qasd qilish o'rtasidagi munosabat qiziqtiradi. Uning aytishicha, bunday harakat yurak sukunatida, xuddi buyuk san'at asari kabi tayyorlanadi va odamning o'zi ko'pincha buni bilmaydi. Bir kuni u harakat qiladi. Gazetalar keyin shaxsiy qayg'ular yoki davosiz kasallik haqida yozadi — bu rost bo'lishi mumkin, lekin haqiqiy boshlanish yashirin qoladi.

paras.en: He then describes suicide, philosophically, as a kind of confession. To kill oneself is to confess that one has been overtaken by life, or that one does not understand it. It is to admit that life is not worth the trouble. Living is never easy: we go on making the gestures that existence demands for many reasons, the first of which is simply habit. To die by one's own choice means that one has recognised — even instinctively — how ridiculous that habit is, that there is no deep reason for living, that daily agitation is senseless and that suffering is useless.
paras.uz: Keyin u o'z joniga qasd qilishni falsafiy jihatdan o'ziga xos e'tirof sifatida tasvirlaydi. O'zini o'ldirish — hayot sendan o'zib ketganini yoki uni tushunmasligingni tan olish demak. Bu hayot mashaqqatga arzimasligini tan olishdir. Yashash hech qachon oson emas: biz borliq talab qiladigan harakatlarni ko'p sabablarga ko'ra qilishda davom etamiz, ulardan birinchisi — shunchaki odat. O'z tanlovi bilan o'lish esa — hatto instinktiv ravishda bo'lsa ham — bu odatning kulgiliqligini, yashash uchun chuqur sabab yo'qligini, kundalik g'alayon ma'nosiz va azob foydasiz ekanini tan olgani demakdir.

paras.en: Here Camus gives his first description of the feeling of absurdity. As long as the world can be explained — even badly, even with false reasons — we feel at home in it. But when all explanations suddenly fall away, a person feels like a foreigner in his own life. Worse, this exile has no cure: he cannot go back to a lost paradise, and he cannot look forward to a promised one. Camus says that this gap between a person and the life he is living — like an actor who suddenly feels separated from the stage around him — is exactly what the feeling of absurdity is.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Kamyu absurd tuyg'usining ilk tavsifini beradi. Dunyoni tushuntirish mumkin ekan — hatto yomon, hatto soxta sabablar bilan bo'lsa ham — biz unda o'zimizni uydagidek his qilamiz. Lekin barcha tushuntirishlar birdan qulab tushganda, odam o'z hayotida o'zini chet ellikdek his qiladi. Bundan ham yomoni, bu surgunning davosi yo'q: u yo'qotilgan jannatga qaytolmaydi va va'da qilingan jannatni ham kuta olmaydi. Kamyuning aytishicha, inson va u yashayotgan hayot o'rtasidagi bu bo'shliq — atrofidagi sahnadan birdan ajralib qolgandek his qilgan aktyor kabi — aynan absurd tuyg'usidir.

paras.en: Since many healthy people have thought about suicide, Camus says, it is fair to recognise a direct link between this feeling of absurdity and the longing for death. The subject of his essay is exactly that link: does the absurd require death? Should a person who has truly understood that life has no given meaning draw the logical conclusion and leave it? This question must be put before all others, and answered honestly, without dramatic gestures and without easy consolations.
paras.uz: Ko'p sog'lom odamlar o'z joniga qasd qilish haqida o'ylagani uchun, deydi Kamyu, bu absurd tuyg'usi va o'limga intilish o'rtasida bevosita bog'liqlik borligini tan olish adolatli. Uning essesi mavzusi aynan shu bog'liqlik: absurd o'limni talab qiladimi? Hayotning berilgan ma'nosi yo'qligini chinakam tushungan odam mantiqiy xulosa chiqarib, undan ketishi kerakmi? Bu savolni barcha savollardan oldin qo'yish va dramatik imo-ishoralarsiz, oson tasallilarsiz, halol javob berish kerak.

paras.en: Camus points out a strange fact about how people actually behave. Those who deny that life has meaning do not always kill themselves; and those who kill themselves were not always sure that life had no meaning. Thinkers who wrote that life is worthless — he mentions Schopenhauer, who praised suicide while sitting at a well-laid dinner table — often went on living comfortably. Thought and action rarely match. That is why the problem deserves careful logic, and not only feeling.
paras.uz: Kamyu odamlarning amalda qanday yo'l tutishiga oid g'alati bir haqiqatni ko'rsatadi. Hayotning ma'nosini inkor etganlar har doim ham o'zini o'ldirmaydi; o'zini o'ldirganlar esa har doim ham hayot ma'nosiz ekaniga ishonch hosil qilmagan bo'ladi. Hayot qadrsiz deb yozgan mutafakkirlar — u bezatilgan dasturxon yonida o'tirib o'z joniga qasd qilishni maqtagan Shopengauerni eslatadi — ko'pincha qulay yashashda davom etishgan. Fikr va harakat kamdan-kam mos keladi. Shuning uchun bu muammo faqat tuyg'u bilan emas, puxta mantiq bilan ko'rib chiqishga loyiq.

paras.en: Against the logic of the mind, Camus places a deeper fact: the body's attachment to the world. We acquire the habit of living before we acquire the habit of thinking. In the race that brings us daily closer to death, the body always keeps its advance. There is something in our attachment to life that is stronger than all the misery of the world, and the judgement of the body is worth as much as the judgement of the mind. The body draws back before death.
paras.uz: Aql mantig'iga qarshi Kamyu chuqurroq haqiqatni qo'yadi: tananing dunyoga bog'liqligi. Biz fikrlash odatini egallashimizdan oldin yashash odatini egallaymiz. Bizni har kuni o'limga yaqinlashtiradigan poygada tana doimo oldinda boradi. Hayotga bog'liqligimizda dunyoning barcha baxtsizliklaridan kuchliroq nimadir bor va tananing hukmi aqlning hukmi qadar qimmatlidir. Tana o'lim oldida orqaga chekinadi.

paras.en: But there is also, Camus says, a typical move that people make to escape the problem, and he gives it a name: the fatal evasion, which is hope. Hope of another life that one must 'deserve', or the trick of those who live not for life itself but for some great idea that goes beyond life, gives it a meaning and betrays it. He does not attack believers personally; he only notes that hope changes the question instead of answering it. If meaning is placed somewhere else, the problem of this life is not solved, only postponed.
paras.uz: Lekin, deydi Kamyu, odamlar muammodan qochish uchun qiladigan odatiy bir harakat ham bor va u unga nom beradi: halokatli qochish — bu umid. «Munosib bo'lish» kerak bo'lgan boshqa hayotga umid yoki hayotning o'zi uchun emas, hayotdan yuqori turadigan, unga ma'no beradigan va unga xiyonat qiladigan qandaydir buyuk g'oya uchun yashaydiganlarning hiylasi. U dindorlarga shaxsan hujum qilmaydi; u faqat umid savolga javob bermasdan, uni o'zgartirib qo'yishini qayd etadi. Agar ma'no boshqa joyga qo'yilsa, bu hayot muammosi hal qilinmaydi, faqat kechiktiriladi.

paras.en: So the question becomes precise. Camus is not asking 'Is life meaningless?' as a sad complaint. He is asking: if we accept, honestly, that life has no meaning we can prove, how should we live — and must we die? He promises to follow the reasoning to its end, without cheating, and to see whether there is a logic of the absurd that leads all the way to death, or another conclusion. The rest of the essay is that journey.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib savol aniq bo'ladi. Kamyu «Hayot ma'nosizmi?» deb g'amgin nolimayapti. U so'rayapti: agar biz hayotning isbotlab bo'ladigan ma'nosi yo'qligini halol qabul qilsak, qanday yashashimiz kerak — va o'lishimiz shartmi? U mulohazani aldamasdan oxirigacha olib borishga va absurdning o'limgacha olib boradigan mantig'i bormi yoki boshqa xulosami — buni ko'rishga va'da beradi. Essening qolgan qismi — shu sayohat.

chapters.title: Absurd walls (I): how the feeling arrives

paras.en: The second chapter of the first part is called Absurd Walls. Its image is a prison: the walls are the limits that human beings run into whenever they try to find a final meaning. Camus begins with feelings, because, he says, great feelings carry their own universe with them, and the feeling of the absurd is no different. It cannot be defined at first, but it can be recognised. It may strike any person, at any street corner, in the middle of an ordinary day.
paras.uz: Birinchi qismning ikkinchi bobi «Absurd devorlar» deb ataladi. Uning timsoli — qamoqxona: devorlar — insonlar so'nggi ma'noni topishga uringanda har safar duch keladigan chegaralar. Kamyu tuyg'ulardan boshlaydi, chunki, deydi u, buyuk tuyg'ular o'zi bilan o'z olamini olib yuradi va absurd tuyg'usi ham shunday. Uni avvaliga ta'riflab bo'lmaydi, lekin tanib olish mumkin. U har qanday odamni, istalgan ko'cha burchagida, oddiy kun o'rtasida urib yuborishi mumkin.

paras.en: Camus notes that we never know a person completely. There is always something in another human being that escapes us, and yet we know people well enough through their actions and the way they behave. In the same way, the absurd cannot be caught in a single definition, but it can be approached through its signs and through the different situations in which it appears. So instead of a definition he offers a list of moments when the 'walls' become visible.
paras.uz: Kamyu biz hech qachon bir odamni to'liq bilmasligimizni qayd etadi. Boshqa insonda doimo bizdan qochadigan nimadir bor, shunga qaramay, odamlarni ularning harakatlari va yurish-turishi orqali yetarlicha yaxshi bilamiz. Xuddi shunday, absurdni bitta ta'rifga sig'dirib bo'lmaydi, lekin unga belgilar va u paydo bo'ladigan turli vaziyatlar orqali yaqinlashish mumkin. Shuning uchun u ta'rif o'rniga «devorlar» ko'rinib qoladigan lahzalar ro'yxatini taklif qiladi.

paras.en: The first moment is the collapse of routine. Camus describes the daily cycle of a working life: you get up, take the tram, work four hours at the office or the factory, eat, take the tram again, work four more hours, eat, sleep — and Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and the rest follow in the same rhythm. This road is easy to follow most of the time. But one day the question 'why?' rises up, and everything begins in a weariness mixed with astonishment.
paras.uz: Birinchi lahza — kundalik tartibning qulashi. Kamyu mehnat hayotining kundalik aylanishini tasvirlaydi: turasan, tramvayga chiqasan, idorada yoki zavodda to'rt soat ishlaysan, ovqatlanasan, yana tramvayga chiqasan, yana to'rt soat ishlaysan, ovqatlanasan, uxlaysan — va dushanba, seshanba, chorshanba va qolganlari xuddi shu ritmda davom etadi. Bu yo'ldan ko'pincha bemalol yurish mumkin. Lekin bir kuni «nega?» degan savol ko'tariladi va hamma narsa hayrat aralash charchoqdan boshlanadi.

paras.en: This weariness, Camus says, comes at the end of the acts of a mechanical life, but at the same moment it starts the movement of consciousness. It wakes consciousness up and provokes what follows. What follows is either a slow return into the chain of habit, or a final awakening. And at the end of the awakening, in time, comes the consequence: suicide or recovery. Weariness in itself is something sickening, but here, he says, it must be judged good, because everything begins with consciousness and nothing is worth anything except through it.
paras.uz: Bu charchoq, deydi Kamyu, mexanik hayot harakatlari oxirida keladi, lekin ayni lahzada ong harakatini boshlab beradi. U ongni uyg'otadi va keyingi narsalarni qo'zg'atadi. Keyingi narsa esa — yo odatlar zanjiriga sekin qaytish, yo yakuniy uyg'onish. Uyg'onish oxirida esa vaqti kelib oqibat keladi: o'z joniga qasd qilish yoki tiklanish. Charchoqning o'zi ko'ngilni aynitadigan narsa, lekin bu yerda, deydi u, uni yaxshi deb baholash kerak, chunki hamma narsa ong bilan boshlanadi va hech narsa faqat u orqali qadrga ega bo'ladi.

paras.en: The second moment concerns time. In ordinary life we are carried by time, but we live as if the future belongs to us. We say 'tomorrow', 'later', 'when you have a position', 'you'll understand when you're older'. Then a day comes when a person notices that he is thirty. He states his age and, in doing so, he places himself in time. He takes his place on a curve he must travel to its end. He belongs to time, and with a sudden horror he recognises it as his worst enemy.
paras.uz: Ikkinchi lahza vaqtga taalluqli. Oddiy hayotda bizni vaqt olib ketadi, lekin biz kelajak bizniki bo'lgandek yashaymiz. «Ertaga», «keyinroq», «lavozimga ega bo'lganingda», «katta bo'lganingda tushunasan» deymiz. Keyin bir kuni odam o'ttiz yoshga kirganini payqaydi. U yoshini aytadi va shu bilan o'zini vaqtga joylashtiradi. U oxirigacha bosib o'tishi kerak bo'lgan egri chiziqda o'z o'rnini egallaydi. U vaqtga tegishli va to'satdan dahshat bilan uni o'zining eng yomon dushmani deb taniydi.

paras.en: This is the revolt of the flesh, Camus calls it. We wanted tomorrow, while everything in us should have refused it, because tomorrow brings us closer to the end. Living for the future, which is what society and hope teach us, means hurrying towards death. The absurd feeling here is the shock of seeing that our natural way of living contradicts our deepest interest: we spend our days wishing them away.
paras.uz: Kamyu buni tananing isyoni deb ataydi. Biz ertangi kunni istardik, holbuki ichimizdagi hamma narsa uni rad etishi kerak edi, chunki ertangi kun bizni oxirga yaqinlashtiradi. Jamiyat va umid o'rgatganidek, kelajak uchun yashash — o'lim tomon shoshilish demak. Bu yerdagi absurd tuyg'usi — tabiiy yashash tarzimiz eng chuqur manfaatimizga zid ekanini ko'rish zarbasi: biz kunlarimizni ular tezroq o'tib ketishini istab o'tkazamiz.

paras.en: The third moment is the strangeness of the world. Camus asks us to notice how 'thick' and foreign physical things can feel: a stone does not explain itself, it simply is there, closed to us. Even beauty can suddenly turn cold. A landscape we loved — hills, a soft evening sky, a line of trees — can for a moment lose all the meaning we usually give it. Then the world seems to return to what it was long before human beings arrived: indifferent, ancient, and in a quiet way hostile.
paras.uz: Uchinchi lahza — dunyoning begonaligi. Kamyu jismoniy narsalar qanchalik «zich» va begona tuyulishi mumkinligiga e'tibor berishimizni so'raydi: tosh o'zini tushuntirmaydi, u shunchaki bor, bizga yopiq. Hatto go'zallik ham birdan sovuq bo'lib qolishi mumkin. Biz sevgan manzara — tepaliklar, mayin oqshom osmoni, daraxtlar qatori — bir lahzaga biz odatda unga beradigan barcha ma'noni yo'qotishi mumkin. Shunda dunyo insonlar paydo bo'lishidan ancha oldingi holatiga qaytganday tuyuladi: befarq, qadimiy va jimgina dushmanona.

paras.en: For a moment, Camus says, we stop understanding the world. For centuries we understood in it only the shapes and patterns we had put into it ourselves. When we lose the strength to use that trick, the world slips away from us. Its thickness and strangeness — that is the absurd. This experience is not mystical. It is simple and almost physical: a familiar street, a room, a tree suddenly looks like something you have never seen, something that does not care about you at all.
paras.uz: Bir lahzaga, deydi Kamyu, biz dunyoni tushunishdan to'xtaymiz. Asrlar davomida biz unda faqat o'zimiz qo'ygan shakl va naqshlarni tushunganmiz. Bu hiyladan foydalanish kuchini yo'qotganimizda, dunyo bizdan sirg'alib chiqadi. Uning zichligi va begonaligi — mana shu absurd. Bu tajriba mistik emas. U oddiy va deyarli jismoniy: tanish ko'cha, xona, daraxt birdan siz hech qachon ko'rmagan, sizga mutlaqo befarq narsadek ko'rinadi.

paras.en: The fourth moment involves other people. Human beings, too, give off something inhuman. In certain hours of lucidity, Camus says, the mechanical side of their gestures, their meaningless pantomime, makes everything around them look stupid. His example is famous: a man is talking on the telephone behind a glass wall. You cannot hear him, but you see his face moving, his hands gesturing. You wonder why he is alive. This discomfort before the inhumanity of man himself is also the absurd.
paras.uz: To'rtinchi lahza boshqa odamlar bilan bog'liq. Insonlar ham g'ayriinsoniy nimanidir taratadi. Kamyuning aytishicha, ravshanlik soatlarida ularning imo-ishoralaridagi mexaniklik, ma'nosiz pantomimasi atrofidagi hamma narsani ahmoqona ko'rsatadi. Uning misoli mashhur: bir odam shisha devor ortida telefonda gaplashyapti. Siz uni eshitmaysiz, lekin yuzining harakatlanayotganini, qo'llari imo qilayotganini ko'rasiz. Nega u yashayapti, deb o'ylab qolasiz. Insonning o'zidagi g'ayriinsoniylik oldidagi bu noqulaylik ham absurddir.

paras.en: Something similar can happen when we meet ourselves. Camus speaks of the moments when the face in the mirror, or our own face in an old photograph, looks like a stranger's — someone familiar and yet unsettling. He also mentions that a writer of his time had given this feeling a name: 'nausea'. He means Jean-Paul Sartre, whose novel Nausea (1938) describes a man who becomes sick at the bare, meaningless existence of things and of his own body.
paras.uz: O'zimizni uchratganimizda ham shunga o'xshash narsa bo'lishi mumkin. Kamyu ko'zgudagi yuz yoki eski suratdagi o'z yuzimiz begonanikidek — tanish, lekin bezovta qiluvchi kimsanikidek — ko'rinadigan lahzalar haqida gapiradi. U o'z davridagi bir yozuvchi bu tuyg'uga nom berganini ham eslatadi: «ko'ngil aynishi». U Jan-Pol Sartrni nazarda tutadi; uning «Ko'ngil aynishi» (1938) romani narsalarning va o'z tanasining yalang'och, ma'nosiz borlig'idan ko'ngli ayniydigan odamni tasvirlaydi.

paras.en: The last and strongest moment is death. Camus admits that so much has been written about death that it is easy to become dramatic, and yet he finds it astonishing that people live as if nobody really knew they will die. Strictly speaking, we have no experience of our own death; we only see the deaths of others. But that is enough. The plain physical fact — a body that no longer reacts to anything, from which the person has simply gone — is, for Camus, the basic horror that lies under all the others.
paras.uz: So'nggi va eng kuchli lahza — o'lim. Kamyu o'lim haqida shunchalik ko'p yozilganki, dramatik bo'lib qolish oson ekanini tan oladi, shunga qaramay, odamlar go'yo hech kim o'lishini aniq bilmagandek yashashidan hayratlanadi. Aniqrog'i, bizda o'z o'limimiz tajribasi yo'q; biz faqat boshqalarning o'limini ko'ramiz. Lekin bu yetarli. Oddiy jismoniy haqiqat — endi hech narsaga javob bermaydigan, inson shunchaki chiqib ketgan tana — Kamyu uchun boshqa barcha dahshatlar ostida yotgan asosiy dahshatdir.

paras.en: Seen from the point of view of death, every plan and every moral rule looks fragile, because none of them can be justified in advance against the certainty of the end. These, then, are the feelings of the absurd: weariness, time, the strangeness of the world and of people, death. Camus admits that all this has been said many times before. His goal is not to be original, but to take these simple, common experiences seriously and see what follows from them.
paras.uz: O'lim nuqtai nazaridan qaraganda, har qanday reja va har qanday axloqiy qoida mo'rt ko'rinadi, chunki ularning hech birini yakunning muqarrarligi oldida oldindan oqlab bo'lmaydi. Absurdning tuyg'ulari mana shular: charchoq, vaqt, dunyo va odamlarning begonaligi, o'lim. Kamyu bularning hammasi ko'p marta aytilganini tan oladi. Uning maqsadi original bo'lish emas, balki bu oddiy, umumiy tajribalarni jiddiy qabul qilib, ulardan nima kelib chiqishini ko'rish.

chapters.title: Absurd walls (II): the limits of reason

paras.en: After the feelings, Camus turns to the intellect, and here the walls become clearer still. The first act of the mind, he says, is to separate what is true from what is false. But as soon as thought looks at itself, it finds contradictions. He recalls an argument that goes back to Aristotle: if someone says that everything is true, he also affirms the truth of the opposite claim, and so of the falsity of his own; and if he says that everything is false, that statement is false too. Reason, used on itself, spins in a circle.
paras.uz: Tuyg'ulardan keyin Kamyu aqlga murojaat qiladi va bu yerda devorlar yanada aniqroq ko'rinadi. Aqlning birinchi harakati, deydi u, haqni noto'g'ridan ajratish. Lekin fikr o'ziga qarashi bilanoq ziddiyatlarni topadi. U Aristotelga borib taqaladigan dalilni eslaydi: kimdir hamma narsa haq desa, u qarama-qarshi da'voning haqligini ham, demak, o'z da'vosining noto'g'riligini ham tasdiqlaydi; agar hamma narsa noto'g'ri desa, bu gap ham noto'g'ri bo'ladi. O'ziga qarshi ishlatilgan aql doira bo'ylab aylanadi.

paras.en: Behind every effort of thought, Camus sees one deep desire: the longing for unity. To understand the world, for a human being, means to reduce it to human terms, to stamp it with a human seal. A cat's universe is not an anthill's universe. When we say 'everything is thought' or 'everything is matter' or 'everything is God', we are trying to make the world one, so that it can answer us. If the world could love and suffer like us, we would be reconciled with it.
paras.uz: Fikrning har bir urinishi ortida Kamyu bitta chuqur istakni ko'radi: birlikka intilish. Inson uchun dunyoni tushunish — uni inson tushunchalariga keltirish, unga inson muhrini bosish demak. Mushukning olami chumoli uyasining olami emas. «Hamma narsa — fikr», «hamma narsa — materiya» yoki «hamma narsa — Xudo» deganimizda, biz dunyoni bir butun qilishga urinamiz, toki u bizga javob bera olsin. Agar dunyo biz kabi seva va azob chek olganida, biz u bilan yarashgan bo'lardik.

paras.en: Camus calls this desire a nostalgia — a homesickness of the mind for an absolute, for a single principle that would explain everything. He notes that philosophers from Parmenides, who taught that all being is One, onwards, have tried to satisfy it. But every time the mind claims to reach total unity, it contradicts itself, because it still stands outside the unity in order to speak about it. The history of thought, for Camus, is the history of this repeated longing and its repeated defeat.
paras.uz: Kamyu bu istakni nostalgiya — aqlning mutlaqlikka, hamma narsani tushuntiradigan yagona tamoyilga bo'lgan sog'inchi deb ataydi. U butun borliq Birdir, deb o'rgatgan Parmeniddan boshlab faylasuflar uni qondirishga urinib kelganini qayd etadi. Lekin har safar aql to'liq birlikka erishdim deb da'vo qilganda, o'z-o'ziga zid keladi, chunki u birlik haqida gapirish uchun baribir undan tashqarida turadi. Kamyu uchun fikr tarixi — bu takrorlanuvchi sog'inch va uning takrorlanuvchi mag'lubiyati tarixi.

paras.en: So what can a person know for certain? Camus answers very modestly. I know that my heart exists, because I can feel it. I know that this world exists, because I can touch it. There my knowledge ends; everything else is construction. Even my own self escapes me. I can list its many faces — its education, its origins, its passions, its silences — but I cannot add them into one whole. Between the certainty that I exist and the content I try to give that certainty, there is a gap that will never be filled.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, inson nimani aniq bila oladi? Kamyu juda kamtarona javob beradi. Men yuragim borligini bilaman, chunki uni his qilaman. Men bu dunyo borligini bilaman, chunki unga qo'lim tegadi. Bilimim shu yerda tugaydi; qolgan hamma narsa — qurilma. Hatto o'z «men»im ham mendan qochadi. Men uning ko'p qirralarini sanab bera olaman — tarbiyasi, kelib chiqishi, ehtiroslari, sukunatlari — lekin ularni bitta butunga qo'sha olmayman. Mavjudligimga bo'lgan ishonch va bu ishonchga berishga urinayotgan mazmunim o'rtasida hech qachon to'lmaydigan bo'shliq bor.

paras.en: Camus says that, in this sense, the old advice 'know yourself', given by Socrates, is worth as much as the advice 'be virtuous' given in a church: both express a wish and an ignorance at the same time. They show the nostalgia, not the solution. We can describe ourselves endlessly, but we cannot grasp what we are. This is one of the absurd walls: the self, which seems the closest thing to us, is also a stranger.
paras.uz: Kamyuning aytishicha, shu ma'noda Suqrot bergan qadimiy «o'zingni bil» maslahati cherkovda aytiladigan «fazilatli bo'l» maslahati qadar qimmatli: ikkalasi ham bir vaqtning o'zida istakni ham, bilmaslikni ham ifodalaydi. Ular yechimni emas, sog'inchni ko'rsatadi. Biz o'zimizni cheksiz tasvirlay olamiz, lekin nima ekanimizni anglay olmaymiz. Bu absurd devorlardan biri: bizga eng yaqin narsadek tuyuladigan «men» ham begona.

paras.en: What about science? Camus imagines asking science to explain the world. At first it collects facts and lists laws, and he is grateful. Then it tells him that this wonderful, varied world can be reduced to atoms, and atoms to electrons, and it describes an invisible system in which electrons move around a nucleus. He understands that he is being given an image, a picture, almost a poem. The science that was supposed to teach him everything ends in hypothesis and metaphor. It can describe and calculate; it cannot explain why.
paras.uz: Ilm-chi? Kamyu ilmdan dunyoni tushuntirishni so'rashini tasavvur qiladi. Avvaliga u faktlarni to'playdi va qonunlarni sanab beradi, u esa minnatdor. Keyin ilm unga bu ajoyib, rang-barang dunyoni atomlarga, atomlarni esa elektronlarga keltirish mumkinligini aytadi va elektronlar yadro atrofida aylanadigan ko'rinmas tizimni tasvirlaydi. U o'ziga obraz, rasm, deyarli she'r berilayotganini tushunadi. Unga hamma narsani o'rgatishi kerak bo'lgan ilm faraz va metafora bilan tugaydi. U tasvirlay va hisoblay oladi; nega degan savolni tushuntira olmaydi.

paras.en: This is not an attack on science. Camus respects it, and he knows that it is the most honest knowledge we have. His point is only that science, too, stops at a wall: it can tell us how the world behaves, but not what it means, or whether it means anything. The mind that wanted unity and clarity finds itself in front of a world that answers with description, not with reasons. The more we know, the more precisely we measure our ignorance of the essential.
paras.uz: Bu ilmga hujum emas. Kamyu uni hurmat qiladi va u bizdagi eng halol bilim ekanini biladi. Uning fikri faqat shuki, ilm ham devorga borib to'xtaydi: u bizga dunyo qanday harakat qilishini ayta oladi, lekin uning ma'nosini yoki umuman ma'nosi bormi — buni emas. Birlik va ravshanlikni istagan aql o'zini sabablar bilan emas, tasvir bilan javob beradigan dunyo oldida topadi. Qanchalik ko'p bilsak, muhim narsa haqidagi bilmasligimizni shunchalik aniq o'lchaymiz.

paras.en: Now Camus can give his definition. The world, taken by itself, is simply not reasonable, and that is all we can say about it. A human being, taken by himself, has a powerful need for clarity and meaning. The absurd is neither of these alone: it is their collision — the moment when our demand for understanding meets a universe that gives no reply. It depends on both sides equally, and for now it is the only thing that connects them, a tense and uncomfortable connection rather than a friendly one.
paras.uz: Endi Kamyu o'z ta'rifini bera oladi. Dunyoni alohida olsak, u shunchaki aqlga muvofiq emas va u haqda aytish mumkin bo'lgan gap shu. Insonni alohida olsak, unda ravshanlik va ma'noga kuchli ehtiyoj bor. Absurd bularning birortasi emas: u ularning to'qnashuvi — tushunish talabimiz hech qanday javob bermaydigan koinotga urilgan lahza. U ikkala tomonga bir xilda bog'liq va hozircha ularni bog'laydigan yagona narsa — do'stona emas, balki tarang va noqulay bog'liqlik.

paras.en: It is important to see what this definition says and does not say. The world is not absurd by itself; a stone or a star is simply what it is. A human being is not absurd by himself either; wanting to understand is natural. The absurd appears only when the two meet: a creature who asks 'why?' living in a universe that does not answer. Camus will hold on to three terms from now on — the irrational world, the human nostalgia, and the absurd that is born from their meeting — and he will refuse to drop any of them.
paras.uz: Bu ta'rif nimani aytayotgani va nimani aytmayotganini ko'rish muhim. Dunyo o'z-o'zidan absurd emas; tosh yoki yulduz shunchaki o'zi bo'lgan narsa. Inson ham o'z-o'zidan absurd emas; tushunishni istash tabiiy. Absurd faqat ikkalasi uchrashganda paydo bo'ladi: javob bermaydigan koinotda yashaydigan, «nega?» deb so'raydigan mavjudot. Kamyu bundan buyon uchta tushunchani ushlab turadi — aqlga sig'maydigan dunyo, inson sog'inchi va ularning uchrashuvidan tug'iladigan absurd — va ulardan birortasini ham tashlab yuborishni rad etadi.

paras.en: Camus then notes that he is not alone on this ground. A whole family of modern thinkers has started from the same wall of the irrational. He names them one by one. Martin Heidegger describes human existence as 'care' and shows that anxiety in front of death reveals our condition. Karl Jaspers despairs of any complete knowledge and speaks of the 'failure' that every thought meets. Lev Chestov, a Russian thinker, fights against reason all his life, showing through Dostoevsky and Nietzsche that reason cannot save us from suffering.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu bu zaminda yolg'iz emasligini qayd etadi. Zamonaviy mutafakkirlarning butun bir oilasi aynan shu aqlga sig'maslik devoridan boshlagan. U ularni birma-bir sanaydi. Martin Haydegger inson borlig'ini «g'amxo'rlik» (tashvish) deb ta'riflaydi va o'lim oldidagi xavotir holatimizni ochib berishini ko'rsatadi. Karl Yaspers har qanday to'liq bilimdan umidini uzadi va har bir fikr duch keladigan «mag'lubiyat» haqida gapiradi. Rus mutafakkiri Lev Shestov butun umri davomida aqlga qarshi kurashadi, Dostoyevskiy va Nitsshe orqali aql bizni azobdan qutqara olmasligini ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: Kierkegaard, the Danish philosopher, lives the absurd more than anyone: he makes despair a central subject, refuses to hide contradictions, and calls himself a sick man who does not want to be cured too quickly. The phenomenologists, led by Edmund Husserl, give up the classical method of reason and return to describing experience as it is, without claiming to explain it. Max Scheler is mentioned too. All of them, Camus says, begin by recognising the same thing: the world cannot be reduced to reason, and human nostalgia meets a wall.
paras.uz: Daniyalik faylasuf Kyerkegor absurdni hammadan ko'ra ko'proq yashaydi: u umidsizlikni markaziy mavzuga aylantiradi, ziddiyatlarni yashirishni rad etadi va o'zini tez tuzalishni istamaydigan kasal odam deb ataydi. Edmund Gusserl boshchiligidagi fenomenologlar aqlning klassik usulidan voz kechib, tajribani tushuntirishga da'vo qilmasdan, qanday bo'lsa shunday tasvirlashga qaytadi. Maks Sheler ham tilga olinadi. Ularning hammasi, deydi Kamyu, bir xil narsani tan olishdan boshlaydi: dunyoni aqlga keltirib bo'lmaydi va inson sog'inchi devorga uriladi.

paras.en: The question, then, is not where these thinkers start, but where they end. They all stand on the same desert ground of the absurd. Camus wants to know what they do next: do they stay there, honestly, with what they know, or do they find a way to escape? The next chapter answers sharply. In his view, almost all of them escape — and he gives their escape a disturbing name.
paras.uz: Demak, savol bu mutafakkirlar qayerdan boshlashida emas, balki qayerda tugashida. Ularning hammasi absurdning bir xil cho'l zaminida turadi. Kamyu ular keyin nima qilishini bilmoqchi: ular o'z bilganlari bilan halol holda o'sha yerda qoladimi yoki qochish yo'lini topadimi? Keyingi bob keskin javob beradi. Uning fikricha, ularning deyarli hammasi qochadi — va u ularning qochishiga bezovta qiluvchi nom beradi.

chapters.title: Philosophical suicide (I): the leap

paras.en: The third chapter of the first part is called Philosophical Suicide. It starts by stating a rule. Camus has found three terms: the human mind with its longing, the irrational world, and the absurd that comes from their meeting. If the absurd is the only certainty, then the first duty of an honest mind is to keep it — not to destroy any of its three terms. To suppress the human longing would be to kill consciousness; to pretend that the world is rational after all would be to lie. Either way, the absurd would disappear, and so would the truth.
paras.uz: Birinchi qismning uchinchi bobi «Falsafiy o'z joniga qasd» deb ataladi. U qoida qo'yish bilan boshlanadi. Kamyu uchta tushunchani topdi: sog'inchi bilan inson aqli, aqlga sig'maydigan dunyo va ularning uchrashuvidan kelib chiqadigan absurd. Agar absurd yagona aniq narsa bo'lsa, halol aqlning birinchi burchi uni saqlab qolish — uning uchta qismidan birortasini ham yo'q qilmaslikdir. Inson sog'inchini bostirish ongni o'ldirish bo'lardi; dunyo baribir aqlli deb ko'rsatish yolg'on bo'lardi. Ikkala holda ham absurd yo'qolardi, u bilan birga haqiqat ham.

paras.en: Camus states this principle like a law of method: a man who has discovered the absurd is bound to it. He cannot go back to the comfortable sleep of habit, and he must not jump to a new comfort either. He must live with what he knows. The whole question becomes: is it possible to live in that tension, without escape? Before he answers, Camus examines the thinkers who, according to him, began from the absurd but did not stay.
paras.uz: Kamyu bu tamoyilni usul qonuni kabi bayon qiladi: absurdni kashf etgan odam unga bog'langan. U odatning qulay uyqusiga qayta olmaydi va yangi qulaylikka ham sakrab o'tmasligi kerak. U bilgani bilan yashashi kerak. Butun savol shunga aylanadi: bu taranglikda, qochmasdan yashash mumkinmi? Javob berishdan oldin Kamyu, uning fikricha, absurddan boshlagan, lekin unda qolmagan mutafakkirlarni tekshiradi.

paras.en: He begins with Karl Jaspers. Jaspers admits that the mind cannot know the world as a whole, and he describes how every attempt at total knowledge ends in failure — a 'shipwreck' of thought. Camus agrees with all this. But then Jaspers takes a step Camus refuses: he finds, in this very failure, the sign of something beyond — 'transcendence', the presence of a hidden being that our failure points to. Nothing in experience justifies this step, Camus says. Jaspers explains nothing; he simply turns the absence of an answer into the proof of an answer.
paras.uz: U Karl Yaspersdan boshlaydi. Yaspers aql dunyoni butunligicha bila olmasligini tan oladi va to'liq bilimga har bir urinish mag'lubiyat — fikrning «halokati» bilan tugashini tasvirlaydi. Kamyu bularning hammasiga qo'shiladi. Lekin keyin Yaspers Kamyu rad etadigan qadamni qo'yadi: aynan shu mag'lubiyatda u narigi tomondagi nimaningdir belgisini — «transsendensiya»ni, mag'lubiyatimiz ishora qiladigan yashirin borliqning mavjudligini topadi. Tajribadagi hech narsa bu qadamni oqlamaydi, deydi Kamyu. Yaspers hech narsani tushuntirmaydi; u shunchaki javob yo'qligini javob borligining isbotiga aylantiradi.

paras.en: Camus calls this a leap. In Jaspers's work, he says, the failure of reason is suddenly declared to be the triumph of a higher reality; the darkness is named light. This is exactly the move that the absurd mind forbids itself. It is not wrong to long for unity, Camus repeats, but it is dishonest to claim we have found it when all we have found is our inability to find it.
paras.uz: Kamyu buni sakrash deb ataydi. Yaspers asarida, deydi u, aqlning mag'lubiyati birdan yuksakroq haqiqatning g'alabasi deb e'lon qilinadi; qorong'ilik yorug'lik deb ataladi. Bu aynan absurd aql o'ziga taqiqlaydigan harakat. Birlikka intilish xato emas, deb takrorlaydi Kamyu, lekin biz topgan narsa faqat uni topa olmasligimiz bo'lsa, uni topdik deb da'vo qilish insofsizlikdir.

paras.en: Next comes Lev Chestov, the Russian thinker whom Camus clearly admires. Chestov spent his life collecting examples of the hopelessness of reason: he loved Dostoevsky's underground man and Nietzsche's rebellion, and he showed that no logic can console a man for his suffering. Up to this point he is a perfect witness of the absurd. But Chestov's conclusion is that precisely where human reason finds no way out, God begins. The only true solution, for him, lies where human judgement sees none. If reason says something is impossible, faith says: then it is possible for God.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu aniq hurmat qiladigan rus mutafakkiri Lev Shestov keladi. Shestov butun umrini aqlning umidsizligiga oid misollar to'plashga sarflagan: u Dostoyevskiyning «yer osti odami»ni va Nitsshening isyonini sevgan va hech qanday mantiq insonni azobidan yupata olmasligini ko'rsatgan. Shu nuqtagacha u absurdning mukammal guvohi. Lekin Shestovning xulosasi shuki, aynan inson aqli chiqish yo'lini topmagan joyda Xudo boshlanadi. Uning uchun yagona haqiqiy yechim inson hukmi hech qanday yechim ko'rmagan joyda yotadi. Agar aql biror narsani imkonsiz desa, iymon aytadi: demak, Xudo uchun mumkin.

paras.en: Camus admires the passion of this position, but he says that Chestov turns the absurd into God. The absurd, which was a confrontation between man and the world, becomes for Chestov the face of an incomprehensible and even inhuman God — a God who may be cruel, contradictory, hateful, and whom one must accept precisely because he is beyond understanding. In this way the absurd is not kept; it is worshipped. And something that is worshipped is no longer a problem: it has become an answer.
paras.uz: Kamyu bu pozitsiyaning ehtirosini qadrlaydi, lekin Shestov absurdni Xudoga aylantiradi, deydi. Inson va dunyo o'rtasidagi to'qnashuv bo'lgan absurd Shestovda tushunib bo'lmaydigan va hatto g'ayriinsoniy Xudoning qiyofasiga aylanadi — shafqatsiz, ziddiyatli, nafratli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan va aynan tushunib bo'lmasligi uchun qabul qilinishi kerak bo'lgan Xudo. Shu tariqa absurd saqlanmaydi; unga sig'iniladi. Sig'iniladigan narsa esa endi muammo emas: u javobga aylangan.

paras.en: Camus's reply is simple. For him the absurd has value only as long as it is not accepted, only as long as the mind keeps facing it. The moment you say 'this is the will of God', the tension disappears, and with it the honesty of the experience. Chestov, he says, knew the absurd better than anyone, and then gave it away. The absurd man, by contrast, recognises the struggle and does not surrender it.
paras.uz: Kamyuning javobi oddiy. Uning uchun absurd faqat qabul qilinmaguncha, faqat aql u bilan yuzma-yuz turishda davom etguncha qadrga ega. «Bu Xudoning irodasi» deganingiz zahoti taranglik yo'qoladi, u bilan birga tajribaning halolligi ham. Shestov, deydi u, absurdni hammadan yaxshiroq bilgan va keyin uni qo'ldan bergan. Absurd inson esa, aksincha, kurashni tan oladi va undan taslim bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: The most important example is Søren Kierkegaard. Camus treats him with great respect and some fascination. Kierkegaard does more than discover the absurd: he lives it. He was full of contradictions, wrote under many false names, broke off his engagement to the woman he loved, described despair as the 'sickness unto death', and refused all comfortable systems of philosophy, especially Hegel's, which claimed to explain everything. If anyone seemed made to remain in the absurd, it was Kierkegaard.
paras.uz: Eng muhim misol — Syoren Kyerkegor. Kamyu unga katta hurmat va qandaydir maftunlik bilan qaraydi. Kyerkegor absurdni kashf etish bilan cheklanmaydi: u uni yashaydi. U ziddiyatlarga to'la bo'lgan, ko'plab soxta ismlar ostida yozgan, sevgan ayoli bilan unashtirishni buzgan, umidsizlikni «o'limgacha bo'lgan kasallik» deb tasvirlagan va falsafaning barcha qulay tizimlarini, ayniqsa hamma narsani tushuntirishga da'vo qilgan Hegel tizimini rad etgan. Agar kimdir absurdda qolish uchun yaratilgandek tuyulgan bo'lsa, bu Kyerkegor edi.

paras.en: And yet, Camus says, Kierkegaard makes the most famous leap of all. He chooses Christianity — not a reasonable Christianity, but a faith that accepts the absurd as its very foundation. He asks for what he calls the sacrifice of the intellect: one must believe because it is absurd. Despair, which was a fact, becomes a sin; the sickness of the mind becomes the path to God. The 'leap' — a word Kierkegaard himself used, later popularised as the 'leap of faith' — is exactly the movement Camus has been describing.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, deydi Kamyu, Kyerkegor eng mashhur sakrashni qiladi. U xristianlikni tanlaydi — aqlga muvofiq xristianlikni emas, balki absurdni o'zining asosi sifatida qabul qiladigan iymonni. U aqlni qurbon qilishni so'raydi: absurd bo'lgani uchun ishonish kerak. Fakt bo'lgan umidsizlik gunohga aylanadi; aql kasalligi Xudoga yo'lga aylanadi. «Sakrash» — Kyerkegorning o'zi ishlatgan, keyinchalik «iymon sakrashi» nomi bilan mashhur bo'lgan so'z — aynan Kamyu tasvirlab kelayotgan harakatdir.

paras.en: Camus answers with one of his sharpest formulas: for Kierkegaard the absurd becomes the criterion of the other world, while for the absurd mind it is only what remains of the experience of this world. He also says that if the absurd is a sin, it is a sin without God. In other words, the absurd man feels exactly the same anguish as the believer, the same separation and the same lack, but he refuses to give it a name that would turn it into salvation. He keeps the wound open rather than covering it with a promise.
paras.uz: Kamyu eng o'tkir formulalaridan biri bilan javob beradi: Kyerkegor uchun absurd narigi dunyoning mezoniga aylanadi, absurd aql uchun esa u faqat shu dunyo tajribasidan qolgan narsadir. U shuningdek, agar absurd gunoh bo'lsa, bu Xudosiz gunoh, deydi. Boshqacha aytganda, absurd inson dindor bilan aynan bir xil iztirobni, bir xil ajralish va bir xil kamchilikni his qiladi, lekin uni najotga aylantiradigan nom berishni rad etadi. U yarani va'da bilan yopishdan ko'ra ochiq qoldiradi.

paras.en: It is important to understand what Camus is not saying. He does not claim that God does not exist; he says he does not know, and that he cannot build a life on what he does not know. He does not mock believers; he calls the leap 'tempting' and understands why people make it. His point is about honesty of thought. A philosophy that begins by proving reason has limits must not end by claiming knowledge beyond those limits. When it does, it kills itself as philosophy.
paras.uz: Kamyu nimani aytmayotganini tushunish muhim. U Xudo yo'q deb da'vo qilmaydi; u bilmasligini va bilmagan narsasi ustiga hayot qura olmasligini aytadi. U dindorlarni masxara qilmaydi; u sakrashni «vasvasali» deb ataydi va odamlar nega uni qilishini tushunadi. Uning fikri — fikrning halolligi haqida. Aqlning chegaralari borligini isbotlashdan boshlangan falsafa o'sha chegaralardan tashqaridagi bilimga da'vo qilish bilan tugamasligi kerak. Agar shunday qilsa, u falsafa sifatida o'zini o'zi o'ldiradi.

paras.en: This is the meaning of the chapter's title. Physical suicide ends a life because life seems meaningless. Philosophical suicide ends a line of thought because its conclusion is unbearable: the thinker reaches the wall of the absurd and then, instead of standing there, jumps over it into hope. In the next chapter Camus shows that the same leap can happen even in a philosophy that has nothing to do with religion — the phenomenology of Husserl — and then he defines the concept precisely.
paras.uz: Bob sarlavhasining ma'nosi shu. Jismoniy o'z joniga qasd hayot ma'nosiz tuyulgani uchun hayotni tugatadi. Falsafiy o'z joniga qasd esa fikr yo'lini tugatadi, chunki uning xulosasiga chidab bo'lmaydi: mutafakkir absurd devoriga yetib keladi, keyin u yerda turish o'rniga, uning ustidan umidga sakraydi. Keyingi bobda Kamyu xuddi shunday sakrash din bilan hech qanday aloqasi bo'lmagan falsafada — Gusserl fenomenologiyasida ham sodir bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi va keyin tushunchani aniq ta'riflaydi.

chapters.recap_uz: Kamyu absurdni «saqlab qolish» qoidasini qo'yadi va Yaspers, Shestov va Kyerkegor qanday qilib absurddan boshlab, oxirida Xudoga yoki transsendensiyaga «sakrab» o'tishini tahlil qiladi. Uning fikricha, bu — absurddan qochish, ya'ni falsafiy o'z joniga qasd.
chapters.note_uz: Kamyu bu mutafakkirlarni hurmat qiladi va ularning boshlang'ich nuqtasiga qo'shiladi. U faqat bitta narsani qabul qilmaydi: qorong'ilikni yorug'lik deb atashni. «Sakrash» so'zi Kyerkegordan olingan va bu bobning kalit atamasi.

chapters.title: Philosophical suicide (II): Husserl and the honest mind
chapters.title_uz: Falsafiy o'z joniga qasd (II): Gusserl va halol aql

paras.en: Not every leap goes towards God. Camus now turns to a very different kind of philosopher, Edmund Husserl, the founder of phenomenology. At first Husserl seems to be the perfect ally of the absurd mind. He gives up the old ambition of explaining the world from one principle. He proposes instead to describe experience exactly as it appears to consciousness, without adding anything. Thinking, for him, is not unifying or reducing; it is learning to look again, carefully, at what is in front of us.
paras.uz: Har bir sakrash ham Xudo tomon yo'nalmaydi. Endi Kamyu butunlay boshqa turdagi faylasufga — fenomenologiya asoschisi Edmund Gusserlga murojaat qiladi. Avvaliga Gusserl absurd aqlning mukammal ittifoqchisidek ko'rinadi. U dunyoni bitta tamoyildan tushuntirishdek eski da'vodan voz kechadi. Buning o'rniga u tajribani ongga qanday ko'rinsa, hech narsa qo'shmasdan, aynan shunday tasvirlashni taklif qiladi. Uning uchun fikrlash — birlashtirish yoki qisqartirish emas; bu oldimizdagi narsaga yana diqqat bilan qarashni o'rganishdir.

paras.en: Camus finds this attractive. Phenomenology, he says, refuses to explain; it only wants to describe. Consciousness, in Husserl's famous idea of 'intentionality', is always consciousness of something — it is like a projector that lights up one object after another without claiming to know what lies behind them. Every object, every moment, has its own value, and none has to be reduced to a deeper hidden truth. This is very close to the absurd attitude: a multitude of experiences, each one real, none of them a sign of something beyond.
paras.uz: Kamyuga bu yoqadi. Fenomenologiya, deydi u, tushuntirishni rad etadi; u faqat tasvirlashni istaydi. Gusserlning mashhur «intensionallik» g'oyasiga ko'ra, ong doimo nimaningdir ongidir — u ortida nima borligini bilaman deb da'vo qilmasdan, narsalarni birin-ketin yorituvchi proyektorga o'xshaydi. Har bir narsa, har bir lahza o'z qadriga ega va ularning hech birini chuqurroq yashirin haqiqatga keltirish shart emas. Bu absurd munosabatga juda yaqin: ko'plab tajribalar, ularning har biri haqiqiy, birortasi ham narigi tomondagi narsaning belgisi emas.

paras.en: But then, Camus says, Husserl goes further. He speaks of 'essences' — eternal forms that every object reveals, which are true in themselves, independent of any mind. He claims that what is true is true absolutely, in itself, even for angels or gods. Suddenly the modest describer has become a builder of eternity. Camus jokes that this gives us an abstract polytheism: not one God, but countless timeless essences, one for each thing, standing behind the world like an army of ideas.
paras.uz: Lekin keyin, deydi Kamyu, Gusserl uzoqroqqa ketadi. U «mohiyatlar» — har bir narsa ochib beradigan, o'z-o'zicha haqiqiy, hech qanday aqlga bog'liq bo'lmagan abadiy shakllar haqida gapiradi. U haqiqat bo'lgan narsa mutlaq, o'z-o'zicha, hatto farishtalar yoki xudolar uchun ham haqiqat, deb da'vo qiladi. Birdan kamtarin tasvirlovchi abadiyat quruvchisiga aylanadi. Kamyu hazil qilib, bu bizga mavhum ko'pxudolikni beradi, deydi: bitta Xudo emas, balki son-sanoqsiz, vaqtsiz mohiyatlar — har bir narsa uchun bittadan — dunyo ortida g'oyalar qo'shinidek turadi.

paras.en: For Camus this is also a leap, but in the opposite direction. Kierkegaard and Chestov humiliate reason in order to reach God. Husserl glorifies reason until it reaches a timeless world of pure truth. One leap goes down, the other goes up, but both leave the ground of human experience. 'Humiliated reason' and 'triumphant reason' meet at the same point: both escape the absurd by declaring that, in the end, there is an answer — whether in faith or in eternal essences.
paras.uz: Kamyu uchun bu ham sakrash, lekin qarama-qarshi yo'nalishda. Kyerkegor va Shestov Xudoga yetish uchun aqlni kamsitadi. Gusserl esa aqlni sof haqiqatning vaqtsiz dunyosiga yetguncha ulug'laydi. Bir sakrash pastga, ikkinchisi yuqoriga ketadi, lekin ikkalasi ham inson tajribasi zaminini tark etadi. «Kamsitilgan aql» va «g'olib aql» bir nuqtada uchrashadi: ikkalasi ham oxir-oqibat javob bor — iymonda yoki abadiy mohiyatlarda — deb e'lon qilib, absurddan qochadi.

paras.en: Here Camus gives his precise definition. Philosophical suicide is the movement by which a thought denies itself and tries to go beyond itself in that very denial. It begins with an honest recognition of limits, and it ends by using those limits as a springboard into what cannot be known. The thinker does not stop thinking, but he stops being faithful to what he has actually discovered. That is why Camus calls it suicide: it is the death of lucidity.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Kamyu aniq ta'rifini beradi. Falsafiy o'z joniga qasd — fikr o'zini inkor etadigan va aynan shu inkor ichida o'zidan oshib o'tishga urinadigan harakat. U chegaralarni halol tan olishdan boshlanadi va o'sha chegaralarni bilib bo'lmaydigan narsaga sakrash uchun tramplin sifatida ishlatish bilan tugaydi. Mutafakkir fikrlashdan to'xtamaydi, lekin haqiqatan kashf etgan narsasiga sodiq bo'lishdan to'xtaydi. Shuning uchun Kamyu buni o'z joniga qasd deb ataydi: bu ravshanlikning o'limi.

paras.en: What does the absurd mind do instead? It does not deny reason; Camus insists on this. Reason is a tool, and a very good one, inside its proper field. The absurd mind simply recognises the limits of that field. It says: here I can know, there I cannot. It does not make the unknown into a god, and it does not make reason into a god either. It stays exactly on the border, and it keeps both its desire for clarity and its knowledge that clarity will not be total.
paras.uz: Absurd aql buning o'rniga nima qiladi? U aqlni inkor etmaydi; Kamyu bunda qat'iy turadi. Aql — o'z sohasida juda yaxshi qurol. Absurd aql shunchaki bu sohaning chegaralarini tan oladi. U aytadi: bu yerda bila olaman, u yerda bila olmayman. U noma'lumni xudoga aylantirmaydi, aqlni ham xudoga aylantirmaydi. U aynan chegarada turadi va ravshanlikka intilishini ham, ravshanlik to'liq bo'lmasligini bilishini ham saqlaydi.

paras.en: Camus describes the absurd man with a series of refusals. He refuses to hope. He refuses to cheat. He refuses to explain everything, and he refuses to explain nothing at all. What remains, after these refusals, is not emptiness but a demanding kind of honesty: the decision to live only with what one knows, to arrange one's life according to it, and to bring in nothing that is not certain. Camus calls this living 'without appeal' — without turning to a higher court that would change the verdict.
paras.uz: Kamyu absurd insonni bir qator rad etishlar orqali tasvirlaydi. U umid qilishni rad etadi. Aldashni rad etadi. Hamma narsani tushuntirishni ham, hech narsani tushuntirmaslikni ham rad etadi. Bu rad etishlardan keyin qoladigan narsa — bo'shliq emas, balki talabchan halollik: faqat bilgan narsa bilan yashash, hayotni unga ko'ra tartibga solish va aniq bo'lmagan hech narsani olib kirmaslik qarori. Kamyu buni «murojaatsiz» yashash deb ataydi — hukmni o'zgartiradigan yuqori sudga murojaat qilmasdan.

paras.en: This is harder than it sounds. Most people, Camus suggests, live with half-measures: they know their life is limited, but they behave as if a final reward or a final meaning were waiting. The absurd man gives up that comfort without bitterness. He does not say 'everything is meaningless, so nothing matters'. He says: 'I do not know if there is a meaning beyond this life, so I will give full weight to this life'. The emphasis moves from the hidden to the visible, from the future to the present.
paras.uz: Bu tuyulganidan qiyinroq. Ko'pchilik odamlar, deydi Kamyu, chala choralar bilan yashaydi: ular hayotlari cheklangan ekanini bilishadi, lekin go'yo oxirida mukofot yoki so'nggi ma'no kutayotgandek yo'l tutishadi. Absurd inson bu qulaylikdan achchiqlanmasdan voz kechadi. U «hamma narsa ma'nosiz, demak hech narsa muhim emas» demaydi. U aytadi: «Bu hayotdan tashqari ma'no bormi, bilmayman, shuning uchun men bu hayotga to'liq og'irlik beraman». Urg'u yashirin narsadan ko'rinadiganiga, kelajakdan hozirgi zamonga ko'chadi.

paras.en: From all this follows an important distinction that runs through the whole book: the absurd is not the same as despair. Despair is a feeling; the absurd is a fact, a condition. One can recognise the absurd without despair, just as one can know that one is mortal without spending every day in terror. Following Camus's logic, the absurd man has no reason to despair, because despair is still a kind of disappointed hope: it assumes that something should have been given and was not. The absurd man expects nothing and therefore loses nothing.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasidan butun kitob bo'ylab o'tadigan muhim farq kelib chiqadi: absurd umidsizlik bilan bir narsa emas. Umidsizlik — tuyg'u; absurd esa — fakt, holat. Absurdni umidsizliksiz tan olish mumkin, xuddi o'lar ekaningni har kuni dahshatda o'tkazmasdan bilish mumkin bo'lganidek. Kamyu mantig'iga ko'ra, absurd insonning umidsizlikka tushishi uchun sabab yo'q, chunki umidsizlik ham hafsalasi pir bo'lgan umidning bir turi: u nimadir berilishi kerak edi, lekin berilmadi, deb taxmin qiladi. Absurd inson hech narsa kutmaydi, shuning uchun hech narsa yo'qotmaydi.

paras.en: Camus's judgement on these philosophers can be summed up like this. They all deserve respect, because they saw the absurd clearly before turning away from it. Their mistake is not stupidity but nostalgia: the human need for a home is so strong that even the greatest minds build one where there is none. The absurd mind feels the same need, but it chooses to live 'homeless' rather than in a house it knows to be imaginary.
paras.uz: Kamyuning bu faylasuflar haqidagi hukmini shunday jamlash mumkin. Ularning hammasi hurmatga loyiq, chunki ular absurddan yuz o'girishdan oldin uni aniq ko'rgan. Ularning xatosi — ahmoqlik emas, balki sog'inch: insonning uyga bo'lgan ehtiyoji shunchalik kuchliki, hatto eng buyuk aqllar ham uy yo'q joyda uy quradi. Absurd aql ham xuddi shu ehtiyojni his qiladi, lekin xayoliy ekanini biladigan uyda yashagandan ko'ra «uysiz» yashashni tanlaydi.

paras.en: Now the question of the first chapter can return in its final form. We have seen that the absurd cannot be escaped through hope without betraying the truth. But can it be escaped through death? If the absurd man refuses philosophical suicide, does he therefore accept physical suicide? Or is there a third way — a way of living that keeps the absurd alive? The next chapter, Absurd Freedom, gives Camus's answer.
paras.uz: Endi birinchi bob savoli o'zining yakuniy shaklida qaytishi mumkin. Biz absurddan umid orqali haqiqatga xiyonat qilmasdan qochib bo'lmasligini ko'rdik. Lekin undan o'lim orqali qochish mumkinmi? Agar absurd inson falsafiy o'z joniga qasdni rad etsa, demak u jismoniy o'z joniga qasdni qabul qiladimi? Yoki uchinchi yo'l bormi — absurdni tirik saqlaydigan yashash tarzi? Keyingi bob — «Absurd erkinlik» — Kamyuning javobini beradi.
