chapters.title: Absurd freedom: revolt, freedom, passion

paras.en: The last chapter of the first part brings the reasoning to its conclusion. Camus starts again from his knowledge, which is very small and very firm. I do not know, he says, whether this world has a meaning that goes beyond it. I know that I cannot know it now. What I can touch and what resists me — that is what I understand. And I know two certainties: my appetite for the absolute and for unity, and the impossibility of reducing this world to a rational principle. Everything else is hope or invention.
paras.uz: Birinchi qismning so'nggi bobi mulohazani xulosasiga yetkazadi. Kamyu yana o'z bilimidan boshlaydi — u juda kichik va juda mustahkam. Bu dunyoning o'zidan tashqariga chiqadigan ma'nosi bormi, bilmayman, deydi u. Hozir buni bila olmasligimni bilaman. Qo'lim tegadigan va menga qarshilik ko'rsatadigan narsa — men tushunadigan narsa shu. Va men ikkita aniq narsani bilaman: mutlaqlik va birlikka bo'lgan ishtiyoqimni hamda bu dunyoni aqliy tamoyilga keltirib bo'lmasligini. Qolgan hamma narsa — umid yoki ixtiro.

paras.en: From these certainties, he draws three consequences. The first is revolt. To live the absurd is first of all to keep it alive, and to keep it alive is to look at it constantly. Revolt, in Camus's special sense, is not a political uprising. It is the permanent confrontation of a human being with his own darkness — an insistence on a clarity that is impossible, a challenge to the world that is renewed every second. It is a refusal to accept, and also a refusal to escape.
paras.uz: Bu aniq narsalardan u uchta oqibat chiqaradi. Birinchisi — isyon. Absurdni yashash — avvalo uni tirik saqlash, uni tirik saqlash esa unga doimo qarab turish demak. Kamyuning o'ziga xos ma'nosidagi isyon siyosiy qo'zg'olon emas. Bu insonning o'z qorong'iligi bilan doimiy yuzma-yuz turishi — imkonsiz ravshanlikni talab qilishda qat'iyat, har soniya yangilanadigan dunyoga da'vat. Bu qabul qilishni rad etish va ayni paytda qochishni ham rad etishdir.

paras.en: Camus compares this revolt to the way danger sharpens our attention. When a person is in danger, everything else falls away and he becomes completely aware. Metaphysical revolt stretches that awareness over the whole of life. It is not hope: it expects nothing. It is the certainty of a crushing fate, but without the resignation that should go with it. The absurd man knows he will lose in the end, and he refuses to lower his eyes.
paras.uz: Kamyu bu isyonni xavf diqqatimizni o'tkirlashtirishiga qiyoslaydi. Odam xavf ostida bo'lganda, qolgan hamma narsa chetga chiqadi va u to'liq hushyor bo'ladi. Metafizik isyon bu hushyorlikni butun hayotga yoyadi. U umid emas: u hech narsa kutmaydi. Bu ezuvchi taqdirning muqarrarligi, lekin u bilan birga kelishi kerak bo'lgan tavakkulsiz. Absurd inson oxirida yutqazishini biladi va ko'zini yerga tushirishni rad etadi.

paras.en: Here, Camus says, we see clearly why the absurd does not lead to suicide. One might think that suicide follows revolt, but it is the opposite. Suicide is acceptance taken to its extreme. It is a confession that one has been beaten; it settles the absurd by ending one of its terms — the human being. In this sense suicide, like the leap, is a way of resolving the absurd, of making it disappear. But the absurd, to stay true, must not be resolved. It escapes suicide to the very extent that it remains conscious and defiant of death.
paras.uz: Shu yerda, deydi Kamyu, nega absurd o'z joniga qasd qilishga olib bormasligini aniq ko'ramiz. Isyondan keyin o'z joniga qasd keladi deb o'ylash mumkin, lekin buning aksi. O'z joniga qasd — oxirgi darajasiga yetkazilgan qabul qilish. Bu yengilganlikni tan olish; u absurdni uning bir qismini — insonni — yo'q qilish bilan hal qiladi. Shu ma'noda o'z joniga qasd ham, sakrash kabi, absurdni hal qilish, uni yo'q qilish yo'li. Lekin absurd haqiqat bo'lib qolishi uchun hal qilinmasligi kerak. U ongli va o'limga qarshi bo'yin egmas bo'lib qolgani darajasida o'z joniga qasddan qochadi.

paras.en: Camus then describes the dignity of this attitude. Revolt, he says, gives life its value. Spread over the whole length of an existence, it restores its greatness. For a person who sees clearly, there is nothing more beautiful than the spectacle of human pride struggling with a reality that is beyond it. The discipline that the mind imposes on itself, the will that refuses to break — these have a power and a beauty of their own. If we pretended that the world were kinder than it is, Camus suggests, we would also make human courage smaller, because that courage only exists in front of a hard reality.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu bu munosabatning qadr-qimmatini tasvirlaydi. Isyon, deydi u, hayotga qadr beradi. Butun bir umr bo'ylab yoyilganda, u hayotning ulug'vorligini tiklaydi. Aniq ko'radigan odam uchun o'zidan ustun turgan haqiqat bilan olishayotgan inson g'ururi manzarasidan go'zalroq narsa yo'q. Aqlning o'ziga yuklagan intizomi, sinishni rad etadigan iroda — bularning o'z kuchi va go'zalligi bor. Agar biz dunyoni aslidagidan mehribonroq deb ko'rsatsak, deydi Kamyu, inson jasoratini ham kichraytirgan bo'lardik, chunki bu jasorat faqat qattiq haqiqat oldidagina mavjud.

paras.en: The second consequence is freedom. Camus is careful here. He is not interested in the classic metaphysical question 'is man free?', because that question only makes sense if there is a master — a God — who could give or take away freedom, and then it immediately becomes the problem of evil. He can know only his own freedom: freedom of thought and freedom of action. And the absurd changes this freedom completely.
paras.uz: Ikkinchi oqibat — erkinlik. Kamyu bu yerda ehtiyotkor. Uni «inson erkinmi?» degan klassik metafizik savol qiziqtirmaydi, chunki bu savol faqat erkinlikni bera yoki tortib ola oladigan xo'jayin — Xudo — bo'lgandagina ma'noga ega va u darhol yovuzlik muammosiga aylanadi. U faqat o'z erkinligini bila oladi: fikr erkinligi va harakat erkinligi. Absurd esa bu erkinlikni butunlay o'zgartiradi.

paras.en: Before he meets the absurd, an ordinary person lives with aims. He thinks about the future, about his career, his old age, his children. He acts as if he were free, as if his life could be directed towards a goal. But all this assumes that tomorrow exists and that there is something to be achieved. The absurd shows that there is no tomorrow in that sense. So the person loses the freedom he believed he had — the freedom to become something, to 'be' a lawyer, a father, a respected man. He discovers that he was a slave to his own plans.
paras.uz: Absurdni uchratishdan oldin oddiy odam maqsadlar bilan yashaydi. U kelajak, kasbi, keksaligi, bolalari haqida o'ylaydi. U go'yo erkin bo'lgandek, go'yo hayotini maqsad sari yo'naltirish mumkin bo'lgandek harakat qiladi. Lekin bularning hammasi ertangi kun borligini va erishiladigan nimadir borligini taxmin qiladi. Absurd bu ma'nodagi ertangi kun yo'qligini ko'rsatadi. Shunday qilib, odam o'zida bor deb ishongan erkinlikni — nimadir bo'lish, advokat, ota, hurmatli odam «bo'lish» erkinligini yo'qotadi. U o'z rejalarining quli bo'lganini kashf etadi.

paras.en: But in losing this false freedom, he gains a deeper one. Freed from the future, he is freed from the rules that the future imposed. Camus compares him to two figures. The first is the mystic, who finds freedom by giving himself up completely, and in that surrender becomes indifferent to everything else. The second is the man condemned to death. Camus speaks of the strange freedom of a prisoner who, at dawn, sees the prison gates open before his execution: nothing matters to him any more except the pure flame of life itself.
paras.uz: Lekin bu soxta erkinlikni yo'qotib, u chuqurroq erkinlikka ega bo'ladi. Kelajakdan ozod bo'lib, u kelajak yuklagan qoidalardan ozod bo'ladi. Kamyu uni ikki qiyofaga qiyoslaydi. Birinchisi — o'zini butunlay topshirish orqali erkinlik topadigan va bu taslimiyatda qolgan hamma narsaga befarq bo'lib qoladigan mistik. Ikkinchisi — o'limga hukm qilingan odam. Kamyu tong saharda, qatldan oldin qamoqxona darvozalari ochilganini ko'rgan mahbusning g'alati erkinligi haqida gapiradi: unga endi hayotning sof alangasidan boshqa hech narsa muhim emas.

paras.en: This, Camus says, is the freedom of the absurd man. For Camus, it is precisely the awareness of death and of the absurd that makes possible the only freedom a human being can really experience and live. The absurd man looks at his life as a condemned man looks at the last hours — not with fear, but with a burning attention to everything that is here and now. He is 'available' for life in a way that someone busy with plans and hopes can never be.
paras.uz: Bu, deydi Kamyu, absurd insonning erkinligi. Kamyu uchun aynan o'lim va absurdni anglash inson haqiqatan boshdan kechira oladigan va yashay oladigan yagona erkinlikni mumkin qiladi. Absurd inson o'z hayotiga o'limga hukm qilingan odam so'nggi soatlarga qaragandek qaraydi — qo'rquv bilan emas, balki hozir va shu yerdagi hamma narsaga yonuvchi diqqat bilan. U hayot uchun rejalar va umidlar bilan band odam hech qachon bo'la olmaydigan darajada «ochiq».

paras.en: The third consequence is passion. If there is no scale of values given from above, if no experience is 'better' in an eternal sense than another, then what matters is not the quality of experiences but their quantity — and, above all, the consciousness with which they are lived. Camus puts it in a formula that sounds shocking: what counts is not the best living but the most living. He does not mean collecting pleasures. He means being fully present to as much of life as possible.
paras.uz: Uchinchi oqibat — ehtiros. Agar yuqoridan berilgan qadriyatlar shkalasi bo'lmasa, agar hech bir tajriba abadiy ma'noda boshqasidan «yaxshiroq» bo'lmasa, unda muhimi tajribalarning sifati emas, balki ularning miqdori — va, eng avvalo, ular qanday ong bilan yashalgani. Kamyu buni hayratlanarli eshitiladigan formulada ifodalaydi: eng yaxshi yashash emas, eng ko'p yashash muhim. U zavqlar to'plashni nazarda tutmaydi. U hayotning iloji boricha ko'p qismida to'liq hozir bo'lishni nazarda tutadi.

paras.en: He explains this with an example. Two people live the same number of years. The world offers both of them, roughly, the same sum of experiences. The difference lies only in how conscious they are of them. To feel one's life, one's revolt, one's freedom as much as possible — that is to live as much as possible. Where clarity rules, the scale of values becomes useless. Camus also quotes, with pleasure, an eighteenth-century churchman, the Abbé Galiani, who said that the important thing is not to be cured, but to live with one's illnesses.
paras.uz: U buni misol bilan tushuntiradi. Ikki odam bir xil yil yashaydi. Dunyo ikkalasiga ham taxminan bir xil tajribalar yig'indisini taklif qiladi. Farq faqat ular bundan qanchalik ongli ekanida. O'z hayotini, isyonini, erkinligini iloji boricha ko'p his qilish — iloji boricha ko'p yashash demak. Ravshanlik hukmron joyda qadriyatlar shkalasi keraksiz bo'lib qoladi. Kamyu shuningdek XVIII asr ruhoniysi abbat Galianining muhim narsa tuzalish emas, balki kasalliklaring bilan yashash, degan gapini zavq bilan keltiradi.

paras.en: So Camus arrives at the first great conclusion of the essay. From the absurd he draws three consequences — his revolt, his freedom and his passion — using nothing but the activity of consciousness. In this way, he says, he transforms into a rule of life what was an invitation to death, and he refuses suicide. The absurd man will live, not because he has found a meaning, but because life without appeal, lived with open eyes, is enough. The next part of the book asks what such a life might look like.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib Kamyu essening birinchi buyuk xulosasiga keladi. Absurddan u ongning faoliyatidan boshqa hech narsadan foydalanmasdan uchta oqibat chiqaradi — o'z isyoni, erkinligi va ehtirosi. Shu tariqa, deydi u, o'limga chorlov bo'lgan narsani hayot qoidasiga aylantiradi va o'z joniga qasdni rad etadi. Absurd inson yashaydi — ma'no topgani uchun emas, balki murojaatsiz, ko'zlari ochiq holda yashalgan hayot yetarli bo'lgani uchun. Kitobning keyingi qismi bunday hayot qanday ko'rinishi mumkinligini so'raydi.

Natijada o'limga chorlov hayot qoidasiga aylanadi: o'z joniga qasd rad etiladi.

chapters.title: The absurd man: is everything permitted?

paras.en: The second part of the essay is called The Absurd Man. The first part asked whether one can live with the absurd; the answer was yes, in revolt, freedom and passion. Now Camus asks what kind of person lives this way, and what rules, if any, guide him. He opens with a phrase of Goethe's that sums up the attitude: 'My field is time.' The absurd man does not look to eternity. His territory is the limited time he has, and he intends to cultivate all of it.
paras.uz: Essening ikkinchi qismi «Absurd inson» deb ataladi. Birinchi qism absurd bilan yashash mumkinmi, deb so'ragan edi; javob — ha, isyon, erkinlik va ehtirosda. Endi Kamyu bunday yashaydigan odam qanday odam ekanini va uni qanday qoidalar — agar bo'lsa — boshqarishini so'raydi. U bu munosabatni jamlaydigan Gyote iborasi bilan ochadi: «Mening maydonim — vaqt». Absurd inson abadiyatga qaramaydi. Uning hududi — o'zida bor cheklangan vaqt va u uning hammasini ishlov berishni niyat qiladi.

paras.en: The obvious objection comes at once. If there is no God and no eternal scale of values, does it not follow that everything is permitted? Camus recalls the famous cry of Ivan Karamazov in Dostoevsky's novel: 'Everything is permitted.' Many readers take it as a cry of liberation, as if the death of God opened the door to any crime. Camus reads it differently. He says it is not a shout of joy but a bitter statement of fact.
paras.uz: Aniq e'tiroz darhol keladi. Agar Xudo va abadiy qadriyatlar shkalasi bo'lmasa, hamma narsaga ruxsat, degan xulosa kelib chiqmaydimi? Kamyu Dostoyevskiy romanidagi Ivan Karamazovning mashhur xitobini eslaydi: «Hamma narsaga ruxsat». Ko'p o'quvchilar buni ozodlik hayqirig'i deb qabul qiladi, go'yo Xudoning o'limi har qanday jinoyatga eshik ochgandek. Kamyu buni boshqacha o'qiydi. Uning aytishicha, bu quvonch hayqirig'i emas, balki faktning achchiq bayoni.

paras.en: The absurd, Camus explains, does not liberate; it binds. It does not authorise every action. It does not say that crime is good. It only says that all actions are, in the end, equivalent in the eyes of eternity — because there is no eternity watching. This is a very different idea. It does not remove consequences; it removes only the cosmic judge. The absurd man still has to live with what his actions produce in the world and among people.
paras.uz: Absurd, deydi Kamyu, ozod qilmaydi; u bog'laydi. U har qanday harakatga ruxsat bermaydi. U jinoyat yaxshi demaydi. U faqat barcha harakatlar oxir-oqibat abadiyat nazarida teng, deydi — chunki kuzatib turgan abadiyat yo'q. Bu juda boshqa g'oya. U oqibatlarni yo'q qilmaydi; u faqat koinot hakamini olib tashlaydi. Absurd inson baribir harakatlari dunyoda va odamlar orasida keltirib chiqaradigan narsalar bilan yashashi kerak.

paras.en: Camus puts it in a precise way: for the absurd man there can be responsibility, but no guilt. If he does wrong, he must pay; he accepts the consequences. But he does not torture himself with remorse in front of an invisible court. Remorse, in this view, is useless — it looks back to a judge who does not exist. What remains is a clear-eyed calculation of consequences: actions can be judged by what they lead to in this life, not by a sin they commit against heaven.
paras.uz: Kamyu buni aniq ifodalaydi: absurd inson uchun mas'uliyat bo'lishi mumkin, lekin gunoh yo'q. Agar u yomonlik qilsa, to'lashi kerak; u oqibatlarni qabul qiladi. Lekin u ko'rinmas sud oldida o'zini pushaymonlik bilan qiynamaydi. Bu nuqtai nazarda pushaymonlik foydasiz — u mavjud bo'lmagan hakamga orqaga qaraydi. Qoladigan narsa — oqibatlarni aniq ko'z bilan hisoblash: harakatlarni osmonga qarshi qilingan gunoh bilan emas, balki bu hayotda nimaga olib kelishi bilan baholash mumkin.

paras.en: Does this mean the absurd man has no morality? Camus admits that he cannot accept any ready-made moral system, because every such system needs a justification beyond experience. But this does not make him a monster. He can choose to be generous, faithful or kind — only he knows that he chooses, and that no reward waits for him. The only 'morality' the absurd allows, Camus suggests, is one of lucidity and consistency: to act in a way that does not lie about the human condition.
paras.uz: Bu absurd insonning axloqi yo'q degani emasmi? Kamyu u hech qanday tayyor axloq tizimini qabul qila olmasligini tan oladi, chunki har bir bunday tizim tajribadan tashqaridagi asoslashga muhtoj. Lekin bu uni yirtqichga aylantirmaydi. U saxiy, sodiq yoki mehribon bo'lishni tanlashi mumkin — faqat u tanlayotganini va hech qanday mukofot kutmayotganini biladi. Absurd ruxsat beradigan yagona «axloq», deydi Kamyu, ravshanlik va izchillik axloqidir: inson holati haqida yolg'on gapirmaydigan tarzda harakat qilish.

paras.en: This is also where the 'ethics of quantity' from the previous chapter returns. If no experience is better than another in itself, what matters is to live as many experiences as possible, and to live them consciously. Camus is aware that this can sound dangerous or shallow. He insists that quantity here does not mean greed or collecting. It means giving the fullest attention to a life that has no second chance. The greatest richness is to feel one's existence intensely.
paras.uz: Shu yerda oldingi bobdagi «miqdor axloqi» ham qaytadi. Agar hech bir tajriba o'z-o'zidan boshqasidan yaxshiroq bo'lmasa, muhimi — iloji boricha ko'p tajribani va ularni ongli yashash. Kamyu bu xavfli yoki yuzaki eshitilishi mumkinligini biladi. U bu yerda miqdor ochko'zlik yoki to'plash demak emasligini ta'kidlaydi. Bu ikkinchi imkoniyati yo'q hayotga eng to'liq diqqatni berish demak. Eng katta boylik — o'z borlig'ini kuchli his qilish.

paras.en: Camus then explains his method for this part of the book. He will present a few figures who live the absurd in a striking way: the seducer, the actor, the conqueror, and later the creator. He stresses that these are not heroes to imitate and not moral examples. They are illustrations — 'styles of life' — chosen because they push the absurd attitude to an extreme where it becomes easy to see. Any ordinary person, he says, an office worker or a teacher, can live the same attitude in a quieter way.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu kitobning bu qismidagi usulini tushuntiradi. U absurdni yorqin tarzda yashaydigan bir necha qiyofani taqdim etadi: vasvasachi, aktyor, istilochi va keyinroq ijodkor. U bular taqlid qilinadigan qahramonlar ham, axloqiy namunalar ham emasligini ta'kidlaydi. Ular — misollar, «hayot uslublari» — absurd munosabatni oson ko'rinadigan darajada chekkaga olib borgani uchun tanlangan. Har qanday oddiy odam, deydi u, idora xodimi yoki o'qituvchi ham xuddi shu munosabatni sokinroq tarzda yashashi mumkin.

paras.en: What do these figures have in common? Each of them knows that his life is limited and that nothing he does will last forever. Each refuses to escape into hope. And each, in his own domain, multiplies his experience: the seducer through love, the actor through the roles he plays, the conqueror through action in history. They do not deny the absurd; they make it the very material of their lives. In this sense they are, as Camus says, men who are 'without appeal' — they expect no higher court to rescue them.
paras.uz: Bu qiyofalarning umumiy jihati nima? Ularning har biri o'z hayoti cheklangan ekanini va qilgan hech narsasi abadiy qolmasligini biladi. Har biri umidga qochishni rad etadi. Va har biri o'z sohasida tajribasini ko'paytiradi: vasvasachi — muhabbat orqali, aktyor — o'ynagan rollari orqali, istilochi — tarixdagi harakati orqali. Ular absurdni inkor etmaydi; ular uni hayotlarining materialiga aylantiradi. Shu ma'noda ular, Kamyu aytganidek, «murojaatsiz» odamlar — ularni hech qanday yuqori sud qutqarishini kutishmaydi.

paras.en: There is also a note of honesty about the limits of this approach. Camus does not claim that the absurd man is always happy, or that his choices are easy. He describes a demanding attitude: one has to give up both the comfort of hope and the comfort of despair. One must also give up the idea of being 'good' in the eyes of a higher authority. What is left is a human being alone with his acts and their consequences — free, but with nothing to hide behind.
paras.uz: Bu yondashuvning chegaralari haqida halol bir eslatma ham bor. Kamyu absurd inson doimo baxtli yoki uning tanlovlari oson deb da'vo qilmaydi. U talabchan munosabatni tasvirlaydi: umidning qulayligidan ham, umidsizlikning qulayligidan ham voz kechish kerak. Shuningdek, yuqori hokimiyat nazarida «yaxshi» bo'lish g'oyasidan ham voz kechish kerak. Qoladigan narsa — harakatlari va ularning oqibatlari bilan yolg'iz qolgan inson: erkin, lekin orqasiga yashirinadigan hech narsasi yo'q.

paras.en: Finally, Camus warns his reader not to look for a happy ending in this part. These portraits show how far the absurd attitude can go, not where it should stop. They are experiments in living with open eyes. The first of them, and the most provocative, is Don Juan — a figure who, for centuries, has been seen as a symbol of sin. Camus will try to see him without the moral lens, as a man who loves fully and expects nothing.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, Kamyu o'quvchini bu qismda baxtli yakun izlamaslikdan ogohlantiradi. Bu portretlar absurd munosabat qanchalik uzoqqa borishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi, qayerda to'xtashi kerakligini emas. Ular ko'zlarni ochiq tutib yashash tajribalari. Ularning birinchisi va eng kutilmagani — asrlar davomida gunoh timsoli sifatida ko'rilgan Don Juan. Kamyu uni axloqiy ko'zoynaksiz, to'liq sevadigan va hech narsa kutmaydigan odam sifatida ko'rishga harakat qiladi.

chapters.title: Don Juanism

paras.en: The first portrait is Don Juan, the legendary Spanish seducer who appears in plays by Tirso de Molina and Molière, in Mozart's opera Don Giovanni, in poems by Byron and many others. In the traditional story he seduces woman after woman, mocks heaven, and is finally dragged into hell by the statue of a man he killed. For centuries he has been a symbol of sin, or, in the romantic version, of a sad soul searching for an impossible perfect love. Camus wants to look at him in a completely different way.
paras.uz: Birinchi portret — Tirso de Molina va Molyer pyesalarida, Motsartning «Don Jovanni» operasida, Bayron va boshqa ko'plab shoirlar she'rlarida paydo bo'ladigan afsonaviy ispan vasvasachisi Don Juan. An'anaviy hikoyada u ayollarni birin-ketin yo'ldan uradi, osmonni masxara qiladi va oxirida o'zi o'ldirgan odamning haykali tomonidan do'zaxga sudrab ketiladi. Asrlar davomida u gunoh timsoli bo'lib kelgan yoki romantik talqinda — imkonsiz mukammal muhabbatni izlayotgan g'amgin ruh timsoli. Kamyu unga butunlay boshqacha qarashni istaydi.

paras.en: First he rejects the romantic reading. People often say that Don Juan goes from one woman to the next because he is looking for the one total love that would satisfy him forever, and that he is disappointed each time. Camus says no: this makes Don Juan a mystic of love, a man of hope. But Don Juan does not hope. He does not leave a woman because he did not find the absolute in her; he leaves because he already knows there is no absolute to find.
paras.uz: Avval u romantik talqinni rad etadi. Odamlar ko'pincha Don Juan uni abadiy qoniqtiradigan yagona to'liq muhabbatni izlagani va har safar hafsalasi pir bo'lgani uchun bir ayoldan boshqasiga o'tadi, deyishadi. Kamyu yo'q deydi: bu Don Juanni muhabbat mistigiga, umid odamiga aylantiradi. Lekin Don Juan umid qilmaydi. U ayolni unda mutlaqlikni topmagani uchun tark etmaydi; u topiladigan mutlaqlik yo'qligini allaqachon bilgani uchun tark etadi.

paras.en: Camus also rejects the idea that Don Juan is a cold collector who enjoys counting his victims. He loves each woman, Camus insists, with the same passion and each time with his whole self. That is precisely why he must repeat the gift. He is not saying 'I have finally found love'; he is saying 'I love you now, completely' — and he knows that 'now' is all a human being has. Camus asks a provocative question: why should one have to love rarely in order to love a great deal?
paras.uz: Kamyu Don Juan qurbonlarini sanashdan zavqlanadigan sovuq kolleksioner, degan fikrni ham rad etadi. U har bir ayolni, deydi Kamyu, bir xil ehtiros bilan va har safar butun qalbi bilan sevadi. Aynan shuning uchun u bu in'omni takrorlashi kerak. U «nihoyat muhabbatni topdim» demaydi; u «seni hozir, butunlay sevaman» deydi — va «hozir» insonning bor-yo'g'i ekanini biladi. Kamyu provokatsion savol beradi: ko'p sevish uchun nega kam sevish kerak?

paras.en: This is the ethics of quantity applied to love. Don Juan does not believe that one love is deeper or more 'true' because it lasts longer or because it is unique. In Mozart's opera his servant Leporello reads out a catalogue of his master's conquests, with the famous number of 1,003 women in Spain alone. For moralists this list is the proof of his sin. For Camus it is the record of a man who refused to rank experiences, and who said yes to each one as fully as he could.
paras.uz: Bu — muhabbatga tatbiq etilgan miqdor axloqi. Don Juan bir muhabbat uzoqroq davom etgani yoki yagona bo'lgani uchun chuqurroq yoki «haqiqiyroq» deb ishonmaydi. Motsart operasida uning xizmatkori Leporello xo'jayinining zafarlari ro'yxatini o'qiydi — faqat Ispaniyaning o'zida mashhur 1003 ta ayol. Axloqchilar uchun bu ro'yxat uning gunohi isboti. Kamyu uchun esa bu tajribalarni darajalarga ajratishni rad etgan va har biriga iloji boricha to'liq «ha» degan odamning qaydnomasi.

paras.en: Camus then attacks a powerful idea in our culture: the idea of eternal love, the love that literature and religion praise as the highest form. He suggests that what is often called 'love' is a mixture of desire, affection, habit and the wish to possess, and that we give it the noble name of eternity to hide its limits. A love that claims to be forever is, in his view, another form of hope — and often another form of possession, a way of binding another person to oneself.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu madaniyatimizdagi kuchli g'oyaga hujum qiladi: adabiyot va din eng yuksak shakl sifatida maqtaydigan abadiy muhabbat g'oyasiga. U ko'pincha «muhabbat» deb ataladigan narsa istak, mehr, odat va egalik qilish istagining aralashmasi ekanini va biz uning chegaralarini yashirish uchun unga abadiyatning olijanob nomini berishimizni aytadi. Abadiy deb da'vo qiladigan muhabbat, uning fikricha, umidning yana bir shakli — va ko'pincha egalik qilishning yana bir shakli, boshqa odamni o'ziga bog'lash yo'li.

paras.en: Against this he sets another kind of love: a generous love that knows it is brief and exceptional, and that does not try to imprison. Such love, he says, gives without demanding the future. It frees both people instead of chaining them. Don Juan's way of loving is, in this sense, liberating: it brings with it all the faces of the world, and it does not pretend that one face can replace all the others. Camus does not say this love is better for everyone; he says it is the love that matches the absurd.
paras.uz: Bunga qarshi u boshqa turdagi muhabbatni qo'yadi: qisqa va noyob ekanini biladigan va qamashga urinmaydigan saxiy muhabbat. Bunday muhabbat, deydi u, kelajakni talab qilmasdan beradi. U ikki odamni zanjirband qilish o'rniga ozod qiladi. Don Juanning sevish tarzi shu ma'noda ozod qiluvchi: u o'zi bilan dunyoning barcha yuzlarini olib keladi va bitta yuz qolgan hammasining o'rnini bosa oladi deb ko'rsatmaydi. Kamyu bu muhabbat hamma uchun yaxshiroq demaydi; u bu absurdga mos keladigan muhabbat deydi.

paras.en: Don Juan is also not a sad or tragic figure in Camus's reading. He laughs. He knows what he is doing, and he is not ashamed. Camus notes that the dramatists who wanted to punish him always had to bring in heaven, because on earth Don Juan had nothing to regret. He was not a seducer out of cynicism or emptiness; he was a man who found life sufficient and did not ask it to promise anything beyond itself.
paras.uz: Kamyu talqinida Don Juan g'amgin yoki fojiali qiyofa ham emas. U kuladi. U nima qilayotganini biladi va uyalmaydi. Kamyu uni jazolamoqchi bo'lgan dramaturglar har doim osmonni olib kirishga majbur bo'lganini qayd etadi, chunki yer yuzida Don Juanning afsuslanadigan hech narsasi yo'q edi. U kinizm yoki bo'shliq tufayli vasvasachi emas edi; u hayotni yetarli deb topgan va undan o'zidan tashqaridagi hech narsani va'da qilishni so'ramagan odam edi.

paras.en: What about the famous ending? In the legend, the statue of the Commander — the father of a woman Don Juan seduced, killed by Don Juan in a duel — comes to dinner and drags him into the flames of hell. Camus reads this as the revenge of divine reason on a man who ignored it: the stone guest represents all the eternal laws that Don Juan laughed at. But Camus suggests that for Don Juan this punishment changes nothing. He knew that his life would end, and he had chosen to spend it fully.
paras.uz: Mashhur yakun-chi? Afsonada Komandorning haykali — Don Juan yo'ldan urgan ayolning otasi, Don Juan duelda o'ldirgan odam — kechki ovqatga kelib, uni do'zax olovlariga sudrab ketadi. Kamyu buni ilohiy aqlning uni e'tiborsiz qoldirgan odamdan olgan qasosi deb o'qiydi: tosh mehmon Don Juan kulgan barcha abadiy qonunlarni ifodalaydi. Lekin Kamyuning fikricha, Don Juan uchun bu jazo hech narsani o'zgartirmaydi. U hayoti tugashini bilgan va uni to'liq sarflashni tanlagan edi.

paras.en: Camus prefers another ending, closer to the absurd. He imagines Don Juan grown old, living in a monastery cell on a Spanish hillside — some legends connect him with a real nobleman who ended his life in religious devotion. But in Camus's picture he does not pray and he does not repent. He sits at a narrow window and looks at the silent landscape, at the stones and the light. This, Camus suggests, is the true end of an absurd life: not hell, not conversion, but a calm, wordless contemplation of a world that asks nothing.
paras.uz: Kamyu absurdga yaqinroq boshqa yakunni afzal ko'radi. U qarigan Don Juanni ispan tepaligidagi monastir hujrasida yashayotgan holda tasavvur qiladi — ba'zi afsonalar uni umrini diniy xizmatda tugatgan haqiqiy bir zodagon bilan bog'laydi. Lekin Kamyuning tasvirida u ibodat qilmaydi va tavba qilmaydi. U tor deraza yonida o'tirib, jim manzaraga, toshlar va yorug'likka qaraydi. Kamyuning fikricha, absurd hayotning haqiqiy yakuni shu: do'zax ham, din o'zgartirish ham emas, balki hech narsa so'ramaydigan dunyoni xotirjam, so'zsiz tomosha qilish.

paras.en: It is important to read this chapter carefully. Camus is not writing a guide to relationships, and he is not recommending that people abandon each other. He uses Don Juan to test one idea: if there is no eternity, then a love that is honest about time may be more truthful than a love that pretends to be eternal. Many readers find this chapter the most debatable in the book — and that is part of its value. It forces us to ask what we really mean when we promise 'forever'.
paras.uz: Bu bobni diqqat bilan o'qish muhim. Kamyu munosabatlar bo'yicha qo'llanma yozmayapti va odamlarga bir-birini tashlab ketishni tavsiya qilmayapti. U Don Juandan bitta g'oyani sinash uchun foydalanadi: agar abadiyat bo'lmasa, vaqt haqida halol bo'lgan muhabbat abadiy bo'lishga da'vo qiladigan muhabbatdan haqqoniyroq bo'lishi mumkin. Ko'p o'quvchilar bu bobni kitobdagi eng munozarali bob deb biladi — va bu uning qadrining bir qismi. U bizni «abadiy» deb va'da berganimizda aslida nimani nazarda tutayotganimizni so'rashga majbur qiladi.

U har bir ayolni butun qalbi bilan, bir xil ehtiros bilan sevadi va hech narsaga umid qilmaydi. chapters.note_uz: Bu bob ataylab provokatsion: Kamyu klassik «gunohkor» qahramonni absurd hikmat timsoliga aylantiradi. Uni axloqiy maslahat sifatida emas, balki «abadiy muhabbat» g'oyasini tanqid qiluvchi fikr tajribasi sifatida o'qing.

chapters.title: Drama: the actor

paras.en: The second figure is the actor. Camus places at the head of this chapter a line from Hamlet, where the prince says that the play is the thing in which he will catch the conscience of the king. The theatre, in other words, is not just entertainment; it is a place where truth can be shown. And the actor, who lives entirely in that place, is for Camus one of the purest examples of the absurd life.
paras.uz: Ikkinchi qiyofa — aktyor. Kamyu bu bob boshiga «Gamlet»dan satr qo'yadi: unda shahzoda tomosha qirolning vijdonini tutadigan narsa ekanini aytadi. Boshqacha aytganda, teatr shunchaki ko'ngilochar emas; bu haqiqatni ko'rsatish mumkin bo'lgan joy. Butunlay shu joyda yashaydigan aktyor esa Kamyu uchun absurd hayotning eng sof misollaridan biri.

paras.en: Why the actor? Because, Camus says, his kingdom is the perishable. Of all kinds of fame, the actor's is the most short-lived. A writer may hope that his books will be read after his death; a painter may hope that his canvases will hang in museums. But a performance disappears the moment the curtain falls. Before film and recording, nothing remained of the greatest actors except the memories of those who saw them — and those memories died with their owners.
paras.uz: Nega aktyor? Chunki, deydi Kamyu, uning saltanati — o'tkinchi narsa. Shon-shuhratning barcha turlari ichida aktyorniki eng qisqa umrli. Yozuvchi kitoblari o'limidan keyin ham o'qilishiga umid qilishi mumkin; rassom rasmlari muzeylarda osilib turishiga umid qilishi mumkin. Lekin spektakl parda tushgan zahoti yo'qoladi. Kino va yozuvdan oldin eng buyuk aktyorlardan ularni ko'rganlarning xotirasidan boshqa hech narsa qolmagan — bu xotiralar esa egalari bilan birga o'lgan.

paras.en: Camus adds that, from the point of view of the absurd, every fame is short-lived in the end. Even the most famous names will be forgotten when the earth grows cold and humanity disappears. Only the actor accepts this openly. He has chosen an art that knows it will vanish. He does not pretend to work for eternity. He bets everything on the present evening, on the audience in front of him, on the few hours in which he lives.
paras.uz: Kamyu absurd nuqtai nazaridan har qanday shon-shuhrat oxir-oqibat qisqa umrli ekanini qo'shimcha qiladi. Hatto eng mashhur ismlar ham yer sovib, insoniyat yo'qolganda unutiladi. Faqat aktyor buni ochiq qabul qiladi. U yo'qolib ketishini biladigan san'atni tanlagan. U abadiyat uchun ishlayotgandek ko'rsatmaydi. U hamma narsani shu oqshomga, oldidagi tomoshabinlarga, yashayotgan bir necha soatiga tikadi.

paras.en: The actor also teaches something about quantity. In three hours on stage he lives a whole destiny. He travels the whole road of a character — from birth into the play to death at the end — and then the next night he becomes someone else. Camus mentions famous roles: Alceste, the bitter honest man of Molière's The Misanthrope; Phèdre, Racine's queen consumed by forbidden passion; Gloucester in King Lear. In the space of an evening the actor lives a life that took them a lifetime.
paras.uz: Aktyor miqdor haqida ham nimanidir o'rgatadi. Sahnadagi uch soat ichida u butun bir taqdirni yashaydi. U personajning butun yo'lini — pyesaga tug'ilishidan oxiridagi o'limigacha — bosib o'tadi, keyingi kechada esa boshqa odamga aylanadi. Kamyu mashhur rollarni eslatadi: Molyerning «Odamovi»sidagi achchiq halol odam Alsest; taqiqlangan ehtirosda yonib ketgan Rasin malikasi Fedra; «Qirol Lir»dagi Gloster. Bir oqshom ichida aktyor ularga bir umr kerak bo'lgan hayotni yashaydi.

paras.en: This multiplication of lives is the actor's way of living 'the most'. He does not search for the one true self hidden behind the masks. He knows that a human being can contain many lives, and he tries to exhaust as many of them as he can. Camus notes that the actor, more than anyone, learns how much people resemble each other, and how much a single life can be a role played to its end.
paras.uz: Hayotlarning bunday ko'payishi — aktyorning «eng ko'p» yashash usuli. U niqoblar ortida yashiringan yagona haqiqiy «men»ni izlamaydi. U inson ko'plab hayotlarni o'z ichiga olishi mumkinligini biladi va ulardan iloji boricha ko'pini tugatishga harakat qiladi. Kamyu aktyor hammadan ko'proq odamlar bir-biriga qanchalik o'xshashini va bitta hayot qanchalik oxirigacha o'ynalgan rol bo'lishi mumkinligini o'rganishini qayd etadi.

paras.en: Then Camus speaks of the body. The actor's art is to give flesh to a character. He has no other material than his own body and voice: a gesture, a way of walking, a look, a silence. Through these he makes a soul visible. For Camus this is very significant, because the absurd mind trusts only what it can see and touch. In the actor, the inner life does not hide in an invisible world; it appears on the surface, in the body, in front of everyone.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu tana haqida gapiradi. Aktyorning san'ati — personajga tana berish. Uning o'z tanasi va ovozidan boshqa materiali yo'q: imo, yurish tarzi, nigoh, sukunat. Ular orqali u ruhni ko'rinadigan qiladi. Kamyu uchun bu juda muhim, chunki absurd aql faqat ko'ra va ushlay oladigan narsaga ishonadi. Aktyorda ichki hayot ko'rinmas dunyoda yashirinmaydi; u yuzada, tanada, hammaning ko'z oldida paydo bo'ladi.

paras.en: This is why, Camus says, the Church was always suspicious of actors. For centuries actors were treated as people living in sin: in France they could be refused the sacraments and even Christian burial unless they formally gave up their profession. The Church understood, he suggests, that the actor's art is a kind of heresy. It teaches that one can have many souls, and that the soul can be fully expressed in a body that will die. It prefers the multiplicity of the moment to the unity of eternity.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun, deydi Kamyu, cherkov aktyorlarga doimo shubha bilan qaragan. Asrlar davomida aktyorlarga gunohda yashaydigan odamlar sifatida munosabatda bo'lingan: Fransiyada ular kasbidan rasman voz kechmasalar, ularga muqaddas marosimlar va hatto xristian dafni rad etilishi mumkin edi. Kamyuning fikricha, cherkov aktyor san'ati o'ziga xos bid'at ekanini tushungan. U insonning ko'p ruhi bo'lishi mumkinligini va ruh o'ladigan tanada to'liq ifodalanishi mumkinligini o'rgatadi. U abadiyat birligidan ko'ra lahzaning ko'pligini afzal ko'radi.

paras.en: Camus tells the story of Adrienne Lecouvreur, a great French actress of the eighteenth century. On her deathbed she was ready to confess and receive the last rites, but she was required first to renounce her profession, and she refused. She chose her art over the promise of eternal life, and she was denied a Christian burial; her body was buried secretly at night. For Camus this is a perfect absurd act: she preferred what she had truly lived to what she was only promised.
paras.uz: Kamyu XVIII asrning buyuk fransuz aktrisasi Adrienna Lekuvrer haqida hikoya qiladi. O'lim to'shagida u tavba qilishga va so'nggi marosimlarni qabul qilishga tayyor edi, lekin undan avval kasbidan voz kechish talab qilindi va u rad etdi. U abadiy hayot va'dasidan ko'ra o'z san'atini tanladi va unga xristian dafni rad etildi; jasadi tunda yashirincha ko'mildi. Kamyu uchun bu mukammal absurd harakat: u faqat va'da qilingan narsadan ko'ra haqiqatan yashagan narsasini afzal ko'rdi.

paras.en: There is also something painful in the actor's life. He is always ending. Every evening he must die with his character, and every season he must leave behind the roles he loved. Camus speaks of the actor's 'perishable' greatness without sentimentality. The actor knows that he too will be forgotten, and still he gives everything to each performance. This is exactly the attitude Camus admires: full commitment without the illusion of permanence.
paras.uz: Aktyor hayotida og'riqli narsa ham bor. U doimo tugatadi. Har oqshom u personaji bilan birga o'lishi kerak va har mavsumda sevgan rollarini ortda qoldirishi kerak. Kamyu aktyorning «o'tkinchi» buyukligi haqida his-tuyg'uga berilmasdan gapiradi. Aktyor o'zi ham unutilishini biladi va baribir har bir spektaklga hamma narsasini beradi. Bu aynan Kamyu qadrlaydigan munosabat: doimiylik xayolisiz to'liq fidoyilik.

paras.en: For modern readers, it is worth remembering that Camus loved the theatre with his whole heart. In Algiers he founded an amateur company, the Théâtre du Travail and later the Théâtre de l'Équipe; he adapted, directed and acted, and later wrote plays such as Caligula and The Misunderstanding. When he praises the actor, he speaks from experience. For him the stage was one of the few places where human beings are fully, honestly alive in the present moment — and know that it will end.
paras.uz: Bugungi o'quvchilar uchun Kamyu teatrni butun qalbi bilan sevganini eslash foydali. Jazoirda u havaskor truppa — «Mehnat teatri», keyinroq «Jamoa teatri»ni tuzgan; u moslashtirgan, sahnalashtirgan va o'ynagan, keyinroq «Kaligula» va «Anglashilmovchilik» kabi pyesalar yozgan. Aktyorni maqtaganida u tajribasidan gapiradi. Uning uchun sahna insonlar hozirgi lahzada to'liq, halol tirik bo'ladigan — va bu tugashini biladigan kam sonli joylardan biri edi.

Uning shon-shuhrati eng o'tkinchi, lekin u bir kechada ko'plab hayotlarni yashaydi, ruhni tana orqali ifodalaydi va abadiyat o'rniga o'tkinchi san'atni tanlaydi. Kamyu cherkovning aktyorlarga qarshi kurashini va Adrienna Lekuvrerning taqdirini eslaydi.
chapters.note_uz: Kamyuning o'zi teatrni juda sevgan: u Jazoirda havaskor truppa tuzgan, pyesalar yozgan, sahnalashtirgan va o'ynagan. Bu bob — sevgan san'ati haqidagi shaxsiy e'tirof ham.

chapters.title: Conquest: the conqueror

paras.en: The third portrait is the conqueror. Unlike the chapters on Don Juan and the actor, this one is written mostly as a monologue: Camus lets the conqueror speak for himself, in the first person. The tone is proud, direct, almost like a soldier's or a revolutionary's speech. The conqueror explains why he has chosen action rather than contemplation, and why that choice is not a flight from thought but its consequence.
paras.uz: Uchinchi portret — istilochi. Don Juan va aktyor haqidagi boblardan farqli o'laroq, bu bob asosan monolog shaklida yozilgan: Kamyu istilochiga birinchi shaxsda o'zi uchun gapirishga imkon beradi. Ohang mag'rur, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri, deyarli askar yoki inqilobchi nutqiga o'xshaydi. Istilochi nega mushohada o'rniga harakatni tanlaganini va bu tanlov nega fikrdan qochish emas, balki uning oqibati ekanini tushuntiradi.

paras.en: The conqueror begins by rejecting a common prejudice: that people of action are people who have stopped thinking. On the contrary, he says, he knows exactly what he believes, and he believes it firmly. He has seen that there are two great paths: to contemplate eternity, or to act in history. Between the two he has chosen history, because history is something he can see and touch, and eternity is not. He prefers certainties, even small ones, to great hopes.
paras.uz: Istilochi keng tarqalgan xurofotni rad etishdan boshlaydi: harakat odamlari — fikrlashdan to'xtagan odamlar. Aksincha, deydi u, u nimaga ishonishini aniq biladi va bunga qat'iy ishonadi. U ikkita buyuk yo'l borligini ko'rgan: abadiyatni mushohada qilish yoki tarixda harakat qilish. Ikkalasi orasidan u tarixni tanlagan, chunki tarix — ko'ra va ushlay oladigan narsa, abadiyat esa unday emas. U buyuk umidlardan ko'ra kichik bo'lsa ham aniq narsalarni afzal ko'radi.

paras.en: This choice has a deep meaning for him. If there is no God and no life beyond this one, then man is his own end. Everything that matters happens here, among human beings, in their struggles, their cities, their wars and their revolutions. The conqueror throws himself into this human world because it is the only one he is sure of. His field, too, is time — not the eternal time of the saints, but the restless time of history.
paras.uz: Bu tanlov uning uchun chuqur ma'noga ega. Agar Xudo va bu hayotdan tashqari hayot bo'lmasa, inson o'zi o'zining maqsadi. Muhim bo'lgan hamma narsa shu yerda, insonlar orasida — ularning kurashlarida, shaharlarida, urushlari va inqiloblarida sodir bo'ladi. Istilochi o'zini shu inson dunyosiga tashlaydi, chunki u ishonch hosil qilgan yagona dunyo shu. Uning maydoni ham vaqt — avliyolarning abadiy vaqti emas, balki tarixning notinch vaqti.

paras.en: And yet the conqueror is not naive. He knows that action, in itself, is useless. Every empire falls, every victory is temporary, every revolution is followed by another. The only action that would be truly useful would be one that remade human beings and the earth completely, and he knows he will never achieve that. He acts anyway. Camus makes him say that he must behave 'as if' — as if his action mattered — while knowing very clearly that, in the end, nothing will remain of it.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay istilochi sodda emas. U harakat o'z-o'zicha foydasiz ekanini biladi. Har bir imperiya qulaydi, har bir g'alaba vaqtinchalik, har bir inqilobdan keyin boshqasi keladi. Haqiqatan foydali bo'ladigan yagona harakat — insonlar va yerni butunlay qayta yaratadigan harakat bo'lardi va u bunga hech qachon erisha olmasligini biladi. U baribir harakat qiladi. Kamyu unga «go'yo» — go'yo harakati muhimdek — yo'l tutishi kerakligini, shu bilan birga oxir-oqibat undan hech narsa qolmasligini juda aniq bilishini aytdiradi.

paras.en: This is the conqueror's form of revolt. He fights not because he believes he will win in any final sense, but because fighting is the only dignified answer to a fate that will crush him. Camus links this with the idea of human greatness: the conqueror stands on the side of humanity against the gods, against destiny, against death. He does not ask the universe to approve of him. He knows the struggle is unequal, and he chooses it.
paras.uz: Bu — istilochining isyon shakli. U oxir-oqibat g'alaba qozonishiga ishongani uchun emas, balki kurash uni ezadigan taqdirga yagona munosib javob bo'lgani uchun kurashadi. Kamyu buni inson buyukligi g'oyasi bilan bog'laydi: istilochi xudolarga, taqdirga, o'limga qarshi insoniyat tomonida turadi. U koinotdan o'zini ma'qullashni so'ramaydi. U kurash teng emasligini biladi va uni tanlaydi.

paras.en: The conqueror speaks of the human body as the only certainty and the only measure. Ideas, systems and promises come and go, but a man's body, his effort and his suffering are real. He prefers the company of people who fight, suffer and die to any abstract truth. In this sense, he says, the conqueror is close to the gods: not because he is immortal, but because he is conscious enough of his strength to live constantly at its limit, at the height of his powers.
paras.uz: Istilochi inson tanasi haqida yagona ishonch va yagona o'lchov sifatida gapiradi. G'oyalar, tizimlar va va'dalar kelib-ketadi, lekin insonning tanasi, mehnati va azobi haqiqiy. U har qanday mavhum haqiqatdan ko'ra kurashadigan, azob chekadigan va o'ladigan odamlar davrasini afzal ko'radi. Shu ma'noda, deydi u, istilochi xudolarga yaqin: o'lmas bo'lgani uchun emas, balki doimo o'z kuchi chegarasida, qudratining cho'qqisida yashash uchun yetarlicha o'z kuchini anglagani uchun.

paras.en: There is a darker side to this portrait, which Camus does not hide. The conqueror lives among prisons, battles and sacrifices. Many conquerors end their lives in a cell or in defeat. Camus suggests that the conqueror knows this and accepts it: the prison cell is the final place where his lucidity is tested. Even there he can remain on the side of the human being, refusing to beg for forgiveness from the forces that crushed him.
paras.uz: Bu portretning Kamyu yashirmaydigan qorong'iroq tomoni ham bor. Istilochi qamoqxonalar, janglar va qurbonliklar orasida yashaydi. Ko'p istilochilar umrini kamerada yoki mag'lubiyatda tugatadi. Kamyuning fikricha, istilochi buni biladi va qabul qiladi: qamoqxona kamerasi uning ravshanligi sinovdan o'tadigan so'nggi joy. Hatto u yerda ham u uni ezgan kuchlardan kechirim so'rashni rad etib, inson tomonida qolishi mumkin.

paras.en: We should read this chapter with history in mind. Camus wrote it at a moment when Europe was full of 'conquerors' — dictators, generals, revolutionaries — and he himself would soon join the French Resistance. The conqueror of this chapter is not a defender of tyranny. He is closer to the revolutionary or the resistance fighter who knows that his cause may fail, that history may forget him, and who still decides to act for human beings here and now.
paras.uz: Bu bobni tarixni yodda tutib o'qish kerak. Kamyu uni Yevropa «istilochilar» — diktatorlar, generallar, inqilobchilar bilan to'lgan bir paytda yozgan va o'zi tez orada fransuz Qarshilik harakatiga qo'shilgan. Bu bobdagi istilochi zulm himoyachisi emas. U o'z ishi muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'lishi mumkinligini, tarix uni unutishi mumkinligini biladigan va baribir insonlar uchun hozir va shu yerda harakat qilishga qaror qiladigan inqilobchi yoki qarshilik kurashchisiga yaqinroq.

paras.en: Later, in his book The Rebel (1951), Camus would examine much more critically how revolt can turn into murder and how revolutions can create new tyrannies. In The Myth of Sisyphus these dangers are only hinted at. The conqueror here is a figure of energy and lucidity, not yet a figure of political warning. It is useful to keep both books in mind: the second answers questions that the first leaves open.
paras.uz: Keyinroq, «Isyonkor inson» (1951) kitobida Kamyu isyon qanday qilib qotillikka aylanishi mumkinligini va inqiloblar qanday qilib yangi zulmlarni yaratishini ancha tanqidiyroq tekshiradi. «Sizif afsonasi»da bu xavflarga faqat ishora qilinadi. Bu yerdagi istilochi — hali siyosiy ogohlantirish emas, balki g'ayrat va ravshanlik qiyofasi. Ikkala kitobni ham yodda tutish foydali: ikkinchisi birinchisi ochiq qoldirgan savollarga javob beradi.

paras.en: With the conqueror, the gallery of the absurd man is complete. Don Juan lives the absurd through love, the actor through the multiplication of lives, the conqueror through action in history. Camus adds that these are not the only possibilities; he could have chosen others, and every ordinary person can find his own form. What unites them is the same clear knowledge and the same refusal to hope. And above them, he says, stands a figure even more absurd than these three: the creator, the artist. To him the third part of the book is devoted.
paras.uz: Istilochi bilan absurd inson galereyasi tugallanadi. Don Juan absurdni muhabbat orqali, aktyor hayotlarni ko'paytirish orqali, istilochi tarixdagi harakat orqali yashaydi. chapters.title: Absurd creation: philosophy and fiction
chapters.title_uz: Absurd ijod: falsafa va badiiy adabiyot

paras.en: The third part of the essay is called Absurd Creation. Camus begins by asking what keeps the absurd man going. All the lives described so far — the seducer, the actor, the conqueror — are lived in a very thin air, at the edge of what a human being can bear. They need some deep, constant activity to sustain them. Camus's answer is creation. Of all the forms of absurd life, he says, the creator's is the one that gives the greatest joy, and also the most absurd.
paras.uz: Essening uchinchi qismi «Absurd ijod» deb ataladi. Kamyu absurd insonni nima davom ettirishini so'rashdan boshlaydi. Hozirgacha tasvirlangan barcha hayotlar — vasvasachi, aktyor, istilochi — juda siyrak havoda, inson chidashi mumkin bo'lgan narsaning chekkasida yashaladi. Ularni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun qandaydir chuqur, doimiy faoliyat kerak. Kamyuning javobi — ijod. Absurd hayotning barcha shakllari ichida, deydi u, ijodkorniki eng katta quvonch beradi va ayni paytda eng absurdi.

paras.en: He recalls a sentence of Nietzsche's: we have art so as not to die of the truth. For Camus, however, art is not an escape from the absurd truth into beautiful illusions. It is a way of living that truth twice. To create is to live doubly: once in experience, and once again in the work that gives that experience a form. The artist, like the actor, multiplies lives — but he also leaves behind an object that shows them.
paras.uz: U Nitsshening bir jumlasini eslaydi: haqiqatdan o'lib qolmaslik uchun bizda san'at bor. Biroq Kamyu uchun san'at absurd haqiqatdan go'zal xayollarga qochish emas. Bu o'sha haqiqatni ikki marta yashash usuli. Ijod qilish — ikki karra yashash: bir marta tajribada, yana bir marta esa o'sha tajribaga shakl beradigan asarda. Rassom ham, aktyor kabi, hayotlarni ko'paytiradi — lekin u ortida ularni ko'rsatadigan buyumni ham qoldiradi.

paras.en: What kind of art fits the absurd? Camus makes a careful distinction. A work of art, he says, is born when the intelligence gives up the attempt to reason about the concrete and decides instead to show it. The artist does not explain; he describes. He does not offer a hidden meaning behind things; he presents things themselves, with their colour, their weight, their silence. This is very close to what phenomenology tried to do, but without the leap into eternal essences.
paras.uz: Absurdga qanday san'at mos keladi? Kamyu ehtiyotkorona farqlaydi. San'at asari, deydi u, aql aniq narsa haqida mulohaza yuritishdan voz kechib, buning o'rniga uni ko'rsatishga qaror qilganda tug'iladi. Rassom tushuntirmaydi; u tasvirlaydi. U narsalar ortidagi yashirin ma'noni taklif qilmaydi; u narsalarning o'zini — rangi, og'irligi, sukunati bilan — taqdim etadi. Bu fenomenologiya qilishga uringan narsaga juda yaqin, lekin abadiy mohiyatlarga sakrashsiz.

paras.en: In this sense, Camus says, the work of art is the triumph of the flesh. It is a celebration of the visible world, of the body, of appearances. It does not pretend to go beyond them. It embodies an intellectual drama — the drama of a mind that wants to understand and cannot — in images, characters and events. That is why a novel can sometimes say more about the absurd than a philosophical treatise: it does not argue; it makes us live the experience.
paras.uz: Shu ma'noda, deydi Kamyu, san'at asari — tananing g'alabasi. Bu ko'rinadigan dunyoning, tananing, ko'rinishlarning bayrami. U ulardan oshib o'tishga da'vo qilmaydi. U intellektual dramani — tushunishni istaydigan, lekin tushuna olmaydigan aql dramasini — obrazlar, qahramonlar va voqealarda gavdalantiradi. Shuning uchun roman ba'zan absurd haqida falsafiy risoladan ko'ra ko'proq narsa ayta oladi: u bahslashmaydi; u bizni tajribani yashashga majbur qiladi.

paras.en: Here Camus makes a claim that has become famous: the great novelists are philosophical novelists. He lists Balzac, Sade, Melville, Stendhal, Dostoevsky, Proust, Malraux and Kafka. What makes them philosophical is not that they put ideas into their characters' mouths, but that they chose to write in images rather than in arguments. That choice itself, Camus says, reveals a conviction: that explanation is useless, and that the world can only be shown, not proven.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Kamyu mashhur bo'lib ketgan da'voni ilgari suradi: buyuk romanchilar — faylasuf romanchilar. U Balzak, Sad, Melvill, Stendal, Dostoyevskiy, Prust, Malro va Kafkani sanaydi. Ularni faylasuf qiladigan narsa — qahramonlari og'ziga g'oyalar solishi emas, balki dalillar o'rniga obrazlar bilan yozishni tanlagani. Bu tanlovning o'zi, deydi Kamyu, bir ishonchni ochib beradi: tushuntirish foydasiz va dunyoni faqat ko'rsatish mumkin, isbotlab bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: The novel, Camus says, has its own logic, its own reasoning, its own intuitions and assumptions. It is not inferior to philosophy; it is philosophy in another form. A great novel creates a whole universe that obeys its own rules, and in doing so it expresses a vision of the world. But not every vision is absurd. The question is whether the novelist stays faithful to the world as it is, or uses his universe to slip in a hidden consolation.
paras.uz: Roman, deydi Kamyu, o'z mantig'iga, o'z mulohazasiga, o'z sezgilari va farazlariga ega. U falsafadan past emas; u boshqa shakldagi falsafa. Buyuk roman o'z qoidalariga bo'ysunadigan butun bir olamni yaratadi va shu bilan dunyo haqidagi qarashni ifodalaydi. Lekin har bir qarash ham absurd emas. Savol shundaki, romanchi dunyoga qanday bo'lsa shunday sodiq qoladimi yoki o'z olamidan yashirin tasalli kiritish uchun foydalanadimi.

paras.en: So Camus sets out the conditions for an absurd work. The artist must be conscious of his limits. His art must be one in which the concrete means nothing more than itself — where a sunset is a sunset, a death is a death, without being a symbol of salvation. The work must not become a refuge or a source of hope. It must not offer the reader the meaning that life refuses. In short, it must be lucid, as the absurd man is lucid.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib Kamyu absurd asar uchun shartlarni belgilaydi. Rassom o'z chegaralarini anglashi kerak. Uning san'ati aniq narsa o'zidan boshqa hech narsani anglatmaydigan san'at bo'lishi kerak — quyosh botishi quyosh botishi, o'lim o'lim bo'lib qoladi, najot ramziga aylanmaydi. Asar boshpana yoki umid manbaiga aylanmasligi kerak. U o'quvchiga hayot rad etgan ma'noni taklif qilmasligi kerak. Qisqasi, u absurd inson ravshan bo'lganidek ravshan bo'lishi kerak.

paras.en: This also means that the work cannot be the 'goal' of a life, or the thing that justifies it. An absurd artist does not say: 'I suffered, but my book will make it all meaningful.' That would be another form of hope — hope in posterity, in immortality through art. Camus insists that the absurd creator works without this illusion. His work is one more experience among others, not a door to eternity.
paras.uz: Bu, shuningdek, asar hayotning «maqsadi» yoki uni oqlaydigan narsa bo'la olmasligini anglatadi. Absurd rassom «Azob chekdim, lekin kitobim hammasini ma'noli qiladi» demaydi. Bu umidning yana bir shakli bo'lardi — avlodlarga, san'at orqali o'lmaslikka umid. Kamyu absurd ijodkor bu xayolsiz ishlashini ta'kidlaydi. Uning asari abadiyatga eshik emas, balki boshqa tajribalar qatoridagi yana bir tajriba.

paras.en: Camus then asks the decisive question: is it possible to write an absurd novel at all? Can a writer build a whole fictional world and keep it free of hope from beginning to end? It is easy to start from the absurd; many novels do. The hard thing is not to finish with a leap — not to end with a conversion, a redemption, a final explanation. To test this, Camus chooses an author who knew the absurd more deeply than almost anyone, and who wrote about it with passion: Fyodor Dostoevsky.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu hal qiluvchi savolni beradi: umuman absurd roman yozish mumkinmi? Yozuvchi butun bir badiiy dunyo qurib, uni boshidan oxirigacha umiddan xoli saqlay oladimi? Absurddan boshlash oson; ko'p romanlar shunday qiladi. Qiyin narsa — sakrash bilan tugatmaslik: din o'zgartirish, gunohdan forig' bo'lish, yakuniy tushuntirish bilan tugatmaslik. Buni sinash uchun Kamyu absurdni deyarli hammadan chuqurroq bilgan va u haqda ehtiros bilan yozgan muallifni tanlaydi: Fyodor Dostoyevskiy.

paras.en: As readers of WordDrop, we can test Camus's own novel against these rules. The Stranger describes without explaining; its sentences are short and concrete; it gives no hidden meaning to the sun, the sea or the killing on the beach; and at the end Meursault refuses the chaplain's offer of hope and opens himself to 'the gentle indifference of the world'. Whether or not you like the book, you can see that Camus tried to write exactly the kind of work that this chapter describes.
paras.uz: WordDrop o'quvchilari sifatida biz Kamyuning o'z romanini bu qoidalar bilan sinab ko'rishimiz mumkin. «Begona» tushuntirmasdan tasvirlaydi; uning jumlalari qisqa va aniq; u quyoshga, dengizga yoki sohildagi qotillikka yashirin ma'no bermaydi; oxirida esa Merso ruhoniyning umid taklifini rad etadi va o'zini dunyoning mayin befarqligiga ochadi. Kitob sizga yoqadimi yoki yo'qmi, Kamyu aynan shu bob tasvirlagan asarni yozishga harakat qilganini ko'rishingiz mumkin.

chapters.title: Kirilov: the logic of the man-god

paras.en: Camus calls all of Dostoevsky's heroes 'modern' because they question the meaning of life. They are not satisfied with rules or customs; they want to know why they should live at all. For Camus, this makes Dostoevsky the novelist who came closest to the absurd. His characters argue about God, freedom and suicide with the same intensity that other people argue about money or love. So Camus asks: does Dostoevsky stay faithful to the absurd, or does he, too, make the leap?
paras.uz: Kamyu Dostoyevskiyning barcha qahramonlarini «zamonaviy» deb ataydi, chunki ular hayot ma'nosini so'roq qiladi. Ular qoidalar yoki urf-odatlar bilan qanoatlanmaydi; ular umuman nega yashashlari kerakligini bilishni istaydi. Kamyu uchun bu Dostoyevskiyni absurdga eng yaqin kelgan romanchiga aylantiradi. Uning qahramonlari Xudo, erkinlik va o'z joniga qasd haqida boshqa odamlar pul yoki muhabbat haqida bahslashganidek ehtiros bilan bahslashadi. Shuning uchun Kamyu so'raydi: Dostoyevskiy absurdga sodiq qoladimi yoki u ham sakraydimi?

paras.en: He begins with a text from Dostoevsky's Diary of a Writer, a journal he published in the 1870s. There Dostoevsky imagines what he calls a 'logical suicide': a man who, having understood that there is no immortality and that human life is therefore absurd and humiliating, decides calmly to kill himself. The man's reasoning is: if I cannot know why I exist, and nature has condemned me to suffer without reason, then I refuse to be its plaything. Dostoevsky presents this to show where unbelief leads.
paras.uz: U Dostoyevskiyning 1870-yillarda chop etgan jurnali — «Yozuvchi kundaligi»dagi matndan boshlaydi. U yerda Dostoyevskiy «mantiqiy o'z joniga qasd» deb atagan narsani tasavvur qiladi: o'lmaslik yo'qligini va shuning uchun inson hayoti absurd va xo'rlovchi ekanini tushungan odam xotirjamlik bilan o'zini o'ldirishga qaror qiladi. Bu odamning mulohazasi shunday: agar men nega mavjud ekanimni bila olmasam va tabiat meni sababsiz azob chekishga mahkum etgan bo'lsa, men uning o'yinchog'i bo'lishni rad etaman. Dostoyevskiy buni ishonchsizlik qayerga olib borishini ko'rsatish uchun taqdim etadi.

paras.en: The same idea appears with much greater force in the novel The Possessed (also translated as Demons), in the character of Kirilov. Kirilov is an engineer, a quiet and strange young man who belongs to a circle of revolutionaries. He has decided to kill himself, and he has agreed that the group can use his suicide: before dying he will sign a false confession taking the blame for a murder they commit. But his reasons for dying are not political. They are purely philosophical.
paras.uz: Xuddi shu g'oya «Jinlar» romanida, Kirillov qahramonida ancha kuchliroq namoyon bo'ladi. Kirillov — muhandis, inqilobchilar to'garagiga mansub sokin va g'alati yigit. U o'zini o'ldirishga qaror qilgan va guruh uning o'limidan foydalanishiga rozi bo'lgan: o'lishdan oldin u ular sodir etgan qotillik aybini o'z bo'yniga oladigan soxta iqrornomaga imzo chekadi. Lekin uning o'lish sabablari siyosiy emas. Ular faqat falsafiy.

paras.en: Kirilov's reasoning, as Camus reconstructs it, goes like this. If God exists, then everything depends on His will, and I can do nothing against it. If God does not exist, then everything depends on my will, and I am obliged to affirm it. In other words, if there is no God, I am god — the master of my own existence. But how can a man prove that he is master of his existence? Only by the one act that no external power commands: by deciding himself the moment of his death.
paras.uz: Kamyu tiklaganidek, Kirillovning mulohazasi shunday. Agar Xudo mavjud bo'lsa, hamma narsa Uning irodasiga bog'liq va men unga qarshi hech narsa qila olmayman. Agar Xudo mavjud bo'lmasa, hamma narsa mening irodamga bog'liq va men uni tasdiqlashga majburman. Boshqacha aytganda, agar Xudo bo'lmasa, men xudoman — o'z borlig'imning xo'jayini. Lekin inson o'z borlig'ining xo'jayini ekanini qanday isbotlay oladi? Faqat hech qanday tashqi kuch buyurmaydigan yagona harakat bilan: o'limi lahzasini o'zi belgilash bilan.

paras.en: Kirilov therefore wants to kill himself not out of despair but out of a kind of pride and love. He sees himself as the first man to make this act freely, without fear, and he believes that his example will free all humanity from the fear of death that, in his view, created the idea of God in the first place. Camus calls it a 'pedagogical' suicide: an act meant to teach. Kirilov even compares himself to Christ — a man who dies for others, to open a new age.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun Kirillov o'zini umidsizlikdan emas, balki o'ziga xos g'urur va muhabbatdan o'ldirmoqchi. U o'zini bu harakatni erkin, qo'rquvsiz qiladigan birinchi odam deb biladi va uning namunasi butun insoniyatni o'lim qo'rquvidan ozod qiladi, deb ishonadi — uning fikricha, aynan shu qo'rquv birinchi navbatda Xudo g'oyasini yaratgan. Kamyu buni «pedagogik» o'z joniga qasd deb ataydi: o'rgatish uchun mo'ljallangan harakat. Kirillov hatto o'zini Masihga qiyoslaydi — boshqalar uchun, yangi davrni ochish uchun o'ladigan odamga.

paras.en: What fascinates Camus is that Kirilov is not a gloomy or broken man. He loves life. He drinks tea at night, plays with a child's ball, speaks with tenderness about a green leaf, and says that everything is good. He is happy, and that is why he is frightening. His suicide is the extreme conclusion of the absurd reasoning taken literally: a man who has seen through all illusions and decides to prove his freedom absolutely. In this sense, Camus says, Kirilov is an absurd hero.
paras.uz: Kamyuni maftun etadigan narsa — Kirillovning g'amgin yoki singan odam emasligi. U hayotni sevadi. U tunda choy ichadi, bolaning to'pi bilan o'ynaydi, yashil barg haqida mehr bilan gapiradi va hamma narsa yaxshi deydi. U baxtli va aynan shuning uchun qo'rqinchli. Uning o'z joniga qasdi — so'zma-so'z qabul qilingan absurd mulohazaning keskin xulosasi: barcha xayollarni ko'rib o'tgan va erkinligini mutlaq isbotlashga qaror qilgan odam. Shu ma'noda, deydi Kamyu, Kirillov — absurd qahramon.

paras.en: But Camus does not accept Kirilov's conclusion, and the reason is important. The whole first part of the essay showed that suicide, even proud suicide, settles the absurd by destroying one of its terms. Kirilov wants to become god by dying; the absurd man wants to remain a man by living. Camus agrees with Kirilov's starting point — that without God man is responsible for his own life — but he draws the opposite conclusion: that freedom must be proved by living with open eyes, not by ending life.
paras.uz: Lekin Kamyu Kirillov xulosasini qabul qilmaydi va buning sababi muhim. Essening butun birinchi qismi o'z joniga qasd, hatto mag'rur o'z joniga qasd ham, absurdni uning bir qismini yo'q qilib «hal qilishini» ko'rsatdi. Kirillov o'lib xudo bo'lmoqchi; absurd inson esa yashab inson bo'lib qolmoqchi. Kamyu Kirillovning boshlang'ich nuqtasiga — Xudosiz inson o'z hayoti uchun mas'ul ekaniga qo'shiladi, lekin qarama-qarshi xulosa chiqaradi: erkinlikni hayotni tugatish bilan emas, ko'zlarni ochiq tutib yashash bilan isbotlash kerak.

paras.en: Camus then turns to other characters. Stavrogin, the cold, mysterious central figure of The Possessed, lives in indifference and finally hangs himself. Ivan Karamazov, in The Brothers Karamazov, refuses to accept a world in which innocent children suffer; he 'returns his ticket' to God, and his reasoning leads to the formula 'everything is permitted' — and then to madness. These men, Camus says, live the absurd to the end. Dostoevsky shows with terrifying honesty where the thought of a world without God can lead.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu boshqa qahramonlarga o'tadi. «Jinlar»ning sovuq, sirli markaziy qiyofasi Stavrogin befarqlikda yashaydi va oxirida o'zini osadi. «Aka-uka Karamazovlar»dagi Ivan Karamazov begunoh bolalar azob chekadigan dunyoni qabul qilishni rad etadi; u Xudoga «chiptasini qaytaradi» va uning mulohazasi «hamma narsaga ruxsat» formulasiga — keyin esa telbalikka olib boradi. Bu odamlar, deydi Kamyu, absurdni oxirigacha yashaydi. Dostoyevskiy Xudosiz dunyo haqidagi fikr qayerga olib borishi mumkinligini dahshatli halollik bilan ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: And yet, Camus says, the final answer of Dostoevsky's work is not absurd. At the end of The Brothers Karamazov, the young and gentle Alyosha speaks to a group of boys at the funeral of a child, and he promises them that they will all rise again and meet once more. The novelist who posed the absurd questions most sharply answers them with faith in immortality. Camus concludes that Dostoevsky is an existential novelist, not an absurd one: his work begins in the absurd and ends in hope.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, deydi Kamyu, Dostoyevskiy ijodining yakuniy javobi absurd emas. «Aka-uka Karamazovlar» oxirida yosh va muloyim Alyosha bir bolaning dafn marosimida bir guruh o'g'il bolalarga gapiradi va ularga hammalari qayta tirilib, yana uchrashishlarini va'da qiladi. Absurd savollarni eng keskin qo'ygan romanchi ularga o'lmaslikka ishonch bilan javob beradi. Kamyu Dostoyevskiy absurd emas, balki ekzistensial romanchi degan xulosaga keladi: uning asari absurddan boshlanib, umid bilan tugaydi.

paras.en: Camus adds a precise and fair remark. What makes Dostoevsky's work contrary to the absurd is not that it is Christian, but that it announces a future life. One can be a Christian and still be lucid about this world, he suggests; the problem is the promise of another world that changes the meaning of this one. With this, Camus has his answer to the question of the previous chapter. Even the greatest novelist of the absurd made the leap. So the absurd work must be something else — and the next chapter tries to say what.
paras.uz: Kamyu aniq va adolatli izoh qo'shadi. Dostoyevskiy asarini absurdga zid qiladigan narsa uning xristianligi emas, balki kelajakdagi hayotni e'lon qilishi. Inson xristian bo'lib ham bu dunyo haqida ravshan bo'lishi mumkin, deydi u; muammo bu dunyoning ma'nosini o'zgartiradigan boshqa dunyo va'dasida. Shu bilan Kamyu oldingi bob savoliga javob topadi. Hatto absurdning eng buyuk romanchisi ham sakradi. Demak, absurd asar boshqacha bo'lishi kerak — va keyingi bob uning qanday ekanini aytishga harakat qiladi.

chapters.title: Ephemeral creation

paras.en: After Dostoevsky, Camus returns to his own question with more confidence. He has seen that even a great novelist who began with the absurd ended in hope. What, then, would a truly absurd creation look like? His answer is in the title of this chapter: it would be ephemeral creation — creation without tomorrow. The absurd artist does not create in order to be remembered, saved or justified. He creates the way the actor acts and the seducer loves: fully, now, knowing that it will pass.
paras.uz: Dostoyevskiydan keyin Kamyu o'z savoliga ko'proq ishonch bilan qaytadi. U absurddan boshlagan buyuk romanchi ham umid bilan tugaganini ko'rdi. Unda haqiqiy absurd ijod qanday ko'rinadi? Uning javobi bob sarlavhasida: bu o'tkinchi ijod — ertasiz ijod bo'lardi. Absurd rassom esda qolish, najot topish yoki oqlanish uchun yaratmaydi. U aktyor o'ynaganidek va vasvasachi sevganidek yaratadi: to'liq, hozir, o'tib ketishini bilib.

paras.en: This changes the meaning of artistic work. For many people, art is a way to escape death: the book outlives its author, the painting survives the painter. Camus rejects this consolation. Absurd creation, he says, must accept that the work may be forgotten, lost or destroyed, and that this does not matter. He goes so far as to say that the absurd creator should be able to see his work destroyed in a single day while knowing that, in a deep sense, it changes nothing. This is a hard wisdom, and he admits it.
paras.uz: Bu badiiy mehnatning ma'nosini o'zgartiradi. Ko'p odamlar uchun san'at o'limdan qochish yo'li: kitob muallifidan uzoq yashaydi, rasm rassomdan omon qoladi. Kamyu bu tasallini rad etadi. Absurd ijod, deydi u, asar unutilishi, yo'qolishi yoki yo'q qilinishi mumkinligini va bu muhim emasligini qabul qilishi kerak. U hatto absurd ijodkor o'z asarining bir kunda yo'q qilinishini ko'ra olishi va chuqur ma'noda bu hech narsani o'zgartirmasligini bilishi kerak, deydi. Bu og'ir hikmat va u buni tan oladi.

paras.en: Why create at all, then? Because creation is a discipline of consciousness. Camus describes the artist's work as a daily effort, a form of self-mastery, a precise measuring of the limits of truth. Each work is an exercise in lucidity: the artist looks at the world, refuses to explain it, and gives it form. In doing so he keeps the absurd alive. The work does not answer the question; it keeps it open, visible, shaped.
paras.uz: Unda nega umuman yaratish kerak? Chunki ijod — ong intizomi. Kamyu rassomning mehnatini kundalik sa'y-harakat, o'zini boshqarish shakli, haqiqat chegaralarini aniq o'lchash deb tasvirlaydi. Har bir asar — ravshanlik mashqi: rassom dunyoga qaraydi, uni tushuntirishni rad etadi va unga shakl beradi. Shu bilan u absurdni tirik saqlaydi. Asar savolga javob bermaydi; u uni ochiq, ko'rinadigan, shakllangan holda saqlaydi.

paras.en: Camus also insists that one work alone means little. An artist's work must be seen as a whole, as a series in which each piece corrects, completes or contradicts the others. The meaning of a creator's life is not in a single masterpiece that 'explains everything', but in the long sequence of attempts, each one partial. In this way the artist's career resembles Sisyphus's labour: the same effort, renewed again and again, never final.
paras.uz: Kamyu bitta asarning o'zi kam narsani anglatishini ham ta'kidlaydi. Rassom ijodini butunlikda, har bir parcha boshqalarini tuzatadigan, to'ldiradigan yoki ularga zid keladigan silsila sifatida ko'rish kerak. Ijodkor hayotining ma'nosi «hamma narsani tushuntiradigan» yagona durdona asarda emas, balki har biri qisman bo'lgan urinishlarning uzoq ketma-ketligida. Shu tariqa rassomning ijodiy yo'li Sizif mehnatiga o'xshaydi: bir xil sa'y-harakat, qayta-qayta yangilanadi, hech qachon yakuniy emas.

paras.en: This is why Camus says that the creator is the most absurd of all the figures he has described. Don Juan multiplies loves; the actor multiplies roles; the conqueror multiplies actions. The creator does all of this at once, through imagination, and he also leaves a trace — while knowing that the trace is as mortal as he is. He lives doubly, and he is doubly aware of the limits of his life. His joy is real, but it is a joy without illusions.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun Kamyu ijodkor u tasvirlagan barcha qiyofalar ichida eng absurdi, deydi. Don Juan muhabbatlarni ko'paytiradi; aktyor rollarni; istilochi harakatlarni. Ijodkor bularning hammasini bir vaqtda, tasavvur orqali qiladi va iz ham qoldiradi — shu bilan birga bu iz o'zi kabi o'lar ekanini biladi. U ikki karra yashaydi va hayotining chegaralarini ikki karra anglaydi. Uning quvonchi haqiqiy, lekin bu xayolsiz quvonch.

paras.en: Camus warns against a common misunderstanding: the idea that art is a 'sublimation', a way of turning pain into something higher, so that suffering is redeemed by beauty. For him, this is another leap. The absurd work does not redeem anything. A painting of a sunset is not the 'meaning' of the sunset; a novel about a death does not make the death meaningful. The work only shows, with as much precision and passion as possible, what is there.
paras.uz: Kamyu keng tarqalgan anglashilmovchilikdan ogohlantiradi: san'at «sublimatsiya», og'riqni yuksakroq narsaga aylantirish usuli, shunda azob go'zallik bilan oqlanadi, degan g'oyadan. Uning uchun bu yana bir sakrash. Absurd asar hech narsani oqlamaydi. Quyosh botishi rasmi quyosh botishining «ma'nosi» emas; o'lim haqidagi roman o'limni ma'noli qilmaydi. Asar faqat u yerda bor narsani iloji boricha aniqlik va ehtiros bilan ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: There is a link here with thought itself. Camus describes the absurd work as the place where thought gives up its old pride. For centuries thought wanted to be the master of reality, to explain and to rule it. In absurd art, thought agrees to serve: it becomes the intelligence that organises appearances, that arranges images, that 'sees'. Camus repeats an idea he has used before: to think is not to unify, but to learn again how to see, to direct one's consciousness, to make each image a privileged place.
paras.uz: Bu yerda fikrning o'zi bilan bog'liqlik bor. Kamyu absurd asarni fikr o'zining eski g'ururidan voz kechadigan joy deb tasvirlaydi. Asrlar davomida fikr haqiqatning xo'jayini bo'lishni, uni tushuntirishni va boshqarishni istagan. Absurd san'atda fikr xizmat qilishga rozi bo'ladi: u ko'rinishlarni tartibga soladigan, obrazlarni joylashtiradigan, «ko'radigan» aqlga aylanadi. Kamyu oldin ishlatgan g'oyani takrorlaydi: fikrlash — birlashtirish emas, balki qanday ko'rishni qaytadan o'rganish, ongni yo'naltirish, har bir obrazni alohida qadrli joyga aylantirishdir.

paras.en: The great artist, in Camus's view, is therefore first of all a great living being — someone who has lived intensely and seen clearly, and who uses his work as one more way of living. He is not a priest of beauty or a prophet. He is a person who experiences the world and gives that experience a shape, with the same lucidity and the same refusal of consolation that we have seen in the other absurd figures. His creation is his revolt made visible.
paras.uz: Kamyu nazarida buyuk rassom shuning uchun avvalo buyuk tirik inson — kuchli yashagan va aniq ko'rgan va asaridan yashashning yana bir yo'li sifatida foydalanadigan kishi. U go'zallik ruhoniysi yoki payg'ambar emas. U dunyoni boshdan kechiradigan va o'sha tajribaga, boshqa absurd qiyofalarda ko'rganimizdek bir xil ravshanlik va tasallidan bir xil voz kechish bilan, shakl beradigan odam. Uning ijodi — ko'rinadigan bo'lgan isyoni.

paras.en: At the end of the third part Camus looks back at the road he has travelled. He has examined the absurd, refused the leaps of philosophers, drawn the consequences of revolt, freedom and passion, and portrayed the seducer, the actor, the conqueror and the creator. All these, he says, are only images of one attitude: a person who lives without appeal, faithful to what he knows, and who multiplies his experience in a world that has no meaning beyond itself. One image is still missing — the one that will give the book its name.
paras.uz: Uchinchi qism oxirida Kamyu bosib o'tgan yo'liga orqaga qaraydi. U absurdni tekshirdi, faylasuflarning sakrashlarini rad etdi, isyon, erkinlik va ehtiros oqibatlarini chiqardi va vasvasachi, aktyor, istilochi va ijodkorni tasvirladi.
