chapters.title: The Myth of Sisyphus

paras.en: The final part of the essay, only a few pages long, gives the whole book its name. Camus tells an ancient Greek myth and reads it as the perfect image of the absurd man. Sisyphus, the gods decided, would spend eternity pushing a huge rock up to the top of a mountain, only to watch it roll back down under its own weight, again and again, forever. The gods, Camus remarks, had some reason to think that there is no more terrible punishment than useless and hopeless labour.
paras.uz: Essening bor-yo'g'i bir necha sahifalik so'nggi qismi butun kitobga nom beradi. Kamyu qadimgi yunon afsonasini hikoya qiladi va uni absurd insonning mukammal obrazi sifatida o'qiydi. Xudolar Sizif abadiyatni ulkan toshni tog' cho'qqisiga itarib chiqarish bilan o'tkazishini, keyin esa toshning o'z og'irligi bilan pastga dumalab tushishini qayta-qayta, abadiy kuzatishini hukm qildi. Xudolar, deydi Kamyu, foydasiz va umidsiz mehnatdan ko'ra dahshatliroq jazo yo'q deb o'ylashda qandaydir haqli edilar.

paras.en: Who was Sisyphus, and why was he punished? Camus collects the different versions of the legend. In Homer he is the wisest and most prudent of mortals. Other traditions call him a highwayman, a trickster. Camus sees no contradiction here. What all the stories share is his attitude towards the gods: he did not fear them, he tricked them, and he preferred life on earth to anything they could offer. His punishment is the price of that preference.
paras.uz: Sizif kim edi va nega jazolandi? Kamyu afsonaning turli talqinlarini to'playdi. Gomerda u o'lar jonlarning eng donishmand va eng ehtiyotkori. Boshqa rivoyatlar uni yo'lto'sar, ayyor deb ataydi. Kamyu bunda ziddiyat ko'rmaydi. Barcha hikoyalarning umumiy jihati — uning xudolarga munosabati: u ulardan qo'rqmagan, ularni aldagan va ular taklif qila oladigan har qanday narsadan yer yuzidagi hayotni afzal ko'rgan. Uning jazosi — shu afzallikning bahosi.

paras.en: One story, known from ancient sources, says that Sisyphus, king of Corinth, saw Zeus carry off Aegina, the daughter of the river-god Asopus. When the grieving father came looking for her, Sisyphus agreed to tell him what he had seen — if Asopus would give Corinth a spring of fresh water. Camus likes this detail: Sisyphus chose a very earthly good, water for his city, over the favour of the gods, and he paid for betraying their secret.
paras.uz: Qadimgi manbalardan ma'lum bir rivoyatga ko'ra, Korinf shohi Sizif Zevs daryo xudosi Asopning qizi Eginani olib ketayotganini ko'rgan. Qayg'uga botgan ota uni izlab kelganda, Sizif ko'rganini aytishga rozi bo'lgan — agar Asop Korinfga toza suv bulog'ini bersa. Kamyuga bu tafsilot yoqadi: Sizif xudolarning marhamatidan ko'ra juda yerdagi ne'matni — shahri uchun suvni tanladi va ularning sirini oshkor qilgani uchun to'ladi.

paras.en: Another story is even bolder. Sisyphus is said to have captured Death itself and put him in chains, so that for a time nobody on earth could die. The god of the underworld, Pluto, could not bear his empty, silent kingdom, and the god of war was sent to free Death from Sisyphus's hands. In these tales Sisyphus is a rebel against the most basic law of existence: he refuses to let death win without a fight.
paras.uz: Boshqa rivoyat yanada jasurroq. Aytishlaricha, Sizif O'limning o'zini qo'lga olib, zanjirband qilgan, shunda bir muddat yer yuzida hech kim o'la olmagan. Yer osti dunyosi xudosi Pluton o'zining bo'sh, jim saltanatiga chiday olmagan va O'limni Sizif qo'lidan ozod qilish uchun urush xudosi yuborilgan. Bu hikoyalarda Sizif borliqning eng asosiy qonuniga qarshi isyonchi: u o'limning kurashsiz g'alaba qilishiga yo'l qo'ymaydi.

paras.en: The last story is the one Camus loves most. When Sisyphus was about to die, he tested his wife's love: he asked her to throw his body, unburied, into the middle of the public square. When he woke in the underworld, he was angry that she had obeyed an order so contrary to human love, and he got permission from Pluto to return to earth to punish her. But once back in the world, he saw the water and the sun again, felt the warm stones and the sea, and he no longer wanted to go back into the darkness.
paras.uz: So'nggi rivoyat — Kamyu eng sevgani. Sizif o'lish arafasida xotinining muhabbatini sinagan: u xotinidan jasadini ko'mmasdan, shahar maydoni o'rtasiga tashlashni so'ragan. Yer osti dunyosida uyg'onganida, xotini inson muhabbatiga shunchalik zid buyruqqa bo'ysunganidan g'azablangan va uni jazolash uchun yer yuziga qaytishga Plutondan ruxsat olgan. Lekin dunyoga qaytgach, u suv va quyoshni yana ko'rdi, iliq toshlar va dengizni his qildi va endi zulmatga qaytishni istamadi.

paras.en: The gods called him back, warned him, threatened him; he ignored them and lived on for years beside the sea he loved. Finally Hermes — Mercury, the messenger of the gods — had to come and drag him back to the underworld by force, where the rock was waiting. For Camus, this is the key to the character. Sisyphus is an absurd hero not only because of his punishment, but because of what caused it: he loved this world too much to give it up.
paras.uz: Xudolar uni chaqirdi, ogohlantirdi, tahdid qildi; u e'tibor bermadi va sevgan dengizi yonida yana ko'p yillar yashadi. Oxirida xudolar elchisi Germes — Merkuriy — kelib, uni kuch bilan yer osti dunyosiga, toshi kutib turgan joyga sudrab ketishga majbur bo'ldi. Kamyu uchun bu qahramonning kaliti. Sizif faqat jazosi tufayli emas, balki unga nima sabab bo'lgani tufayli absurd qahramon: u bu dunyoni undan voz kecholmaydigan darajada sevgan.

paras.en: Camus sums up the cause of the punishment in three passions: contempt for the gods, hatred of death, and love of life. The punishment fits them exactly: a man who loved action is condemned to an action that achieves nothing. Since myths live through our imagination, Camus asks us to picture the scene ourselves — the body straining against the stone, the effort of the shoulders and legs, the endless repetition under an empty sky. He does not hide how heavy this is.
paras.uz: Kamyu jazoning sababini uchta ehtirosga jamlaydi: xudolarni mensimaslik, o'limga nafrat va hayotga muhabbat. Jazo ularga aynan mos: harakatni sevgan odam hech narsaga erishmaydigan harakatga hukm qilinadi. Afsonalar tasavvurimiz orqali yashagani uchun Kamyu bizni manzarani o'zimiz tasavvur qilishga chaqiradi — toshga qarshi zo'riqqan tana, yelka va oyoqlarning sa'y-harakati, bo'sh osmon ostidagi cheksiz takror. U buning qanchalik og'irligini yashirmaydi.

paras.en: Then Camus does something surprising. He is less interested in the climb than in the walk back down. Each time the rock reaches the summit it rolls away, and Sisyphus has to descend to start again. During that descent his hands are free and his mind is free. Camus calls it a breathing space — and, above all, the hour of consciousness. It is the moment when Sisyphus can look at his whole situation and think about it.
paras.uz: Keyin Kamyu kutilmagan ish qiladi. Uni tepaga chiqishdan ko'ra pastga qaytish ko'proq qiziqtiradi. Har safar tosh cho'qqiga yetganda dumalab ketadi va Sizif qayta boshlash uchun pastga tushishi kerak. Shu tushish paytida uning qo'llari ham, aqli ham bo'sh. Kamyu buni nafas rostlash vaqti — va, eng avvalo, ong soati deb ataydi. Bu Sizif butun holatiga qarab, u haqda o'ylay oladigan lahza.

paras.en: Why is this moment so important? Because the tragedy of the myth depends on the fact that Sisyphus knows. If he believed that one day the rock would stay at the top, his labour would be bearable — but it would also be a lie. He has no such hope. And yet, Camus argues, that same knowledge is what lifts him above his punishment. The gods wanted to crush him with futility; by looking at that futility clearly, without begging, he becomes greater than the fate they designed for him.
paras.uz: Bu lahza nega bunchalik muhim? Chunki afsonaning fojiasi Sizif bilishiga bog'liq. Agar u bir kuni tosh cho'qqida qoladi deb ishonganida, mehnatiga chidash mumkin bo'lardi — lekin bu yolg'on ham bo'lardi. Unda bunday umid yo'q. Shunga qaramay, deydi Kamyu, aynan shu bilim uni jazosidan yuqoriga ko'taradi. Xudolar uni befoydalik bilan ezmoqchi edi; bu befoydalikka yolvormasdan, aniq qarab, u ular o'ylab topgan taqdirdan ulug'roq bo'ladi.

paras.en: Camus immediately brings the myth down to earth. Many people today, he points out, spend their lives repeating the same tasks in factories and offices, and their situation is no less absurd than Sisyphus's. It becomes tragic only when they become aware of it — and it is at that moment that revolt becomes possible. Sisyphus is therefore not a distant figure from mythology. He is the image of any worker, any ordinary person, who suddenly sees his life clearly and refuses to be crushed by that vision.
paras.uz: Kamyu darhol afsonani yerga tushiradi. Bugun ko'p odamlar, deydi u, umrini zavod va idoralarda bir xil vazifalarni takrorlash bilan o'tkazadi va ularning holati Sizifnikidan kam absurd emas. U faqat ular buni anglaganda fojiali bo'ladi — va aynan o'sha lahzada isyon mumkin bo'ladi. Shuning uchun Sizif mifologiyadagi uzoq qiyofa emas. U har qanday ishchining, birdan hayotini aniq ko'rgan va bu manzaraga ezilishni rad etgan har qanday oddiy odamning obrazi.

paras.en: Camus admits that the descent is not always calm. There are days when memories of happiness press too hard, when sadness wins — and on those days the rock is truly victorious. But he believes that a hard truth weighs less once it is fully faced. Here he calls on another figure from Greek tragedy: Oedipus, who at the end of Sophocles' plays, blind and ruined, still declares that all is well. For Camus this is not resignation but the same kind of victory that Sisyphus can win.
paras.uz: Kamyu tushish har doim ham xotirjam emasligini tan oladi. Baxt xotiralari haddan tashqari bosib keladigan, g'am g'olib chiqadigan kunlar bo'ladi — va o'sha kunlari tosh haqiqatan g'olib. Lekin u og'ir haqiqat to'liq yuzma-yuz kelinganda kamroq bosadi, deb ishonadi. Shu yerda u yunon tragediyasidan yana bir qiyofani chaqiradi: Sofokl pyesalari oxirida ko'r va xonavayron bo'lgan, lekin baribir hammasi yaxshi deb e'lon qiladigan Edip. Kamyu uchun bu taslimiyat emas, balki Sizif erisha oladigan xuddi shunday g'alaba.

paras.en: From here Camus draws the joy hidden in the myth. Sisyphus's fate is his own; no god can live it for him, and no god can give it meaning from outside. When he stops waiting for help from above, the world around him becomes simply the world — silent, but full of its own small voices and details. Light and darkness belong together. The absurd man says yes to all of it, keeps working, and knows that, whatever forces are against him, his days are his own.
paras.uz: Bu yerdan Kamyu afsonada yashiringan quvonchni chiqaradi. Sizifning taqdiri o'ziniki; hech bir xudo uni uning o'rniga yashay olmaydi va hech bir xudo unga tashqaridan ma'no bera olmaydi. U yuqoridan yordam kutishni to'xtatganda, atrofidagi dunyo shunchaki dunyoga aylanadi — jim, lekin o'zining kichik ovozlari va tafsilotlariga to'la. Yorug'lik va zulmat birga keladi. Absurd inson bularning hammasiga «ha» deydi, ishlashda davom etadi va qanday kuchlar unga qarshi bo'lmasin, kunlari o'ziniki ekanini biladi.

paras.en: In Camus's final picture, Sisyphus turns back towards the rock and looks at his life: a series of actions that have no meaning given from above, but which together make up his own destiny, created by him and closed only by his death. He knows the night will not end, and he keeps walking. Camus leaves him at the foot of the mountain, about to begin again, because a human being always finds his burden once more.
paras.uz: Kamyuning yakuniy tasvirida Sizif toshiga qaytadan yuzlanadi va hayotiga qaraydi: yuqoridan berilgan ma'nosi yo'q, lekin birgalikda uning o'z taqdirini tashkil etadigan, o'zi yaratgan va faqat o'limi bilan yopiladigan harakatlar silsilasi. U tun tugamasligini biladi va yurishda davom etadi. Kamyu uni tog' etagida, yana boshlash arafasida qoldiradi, chunki inson har doim o'z yukini qaytadan topadi.

paras.en: And then the famous ending. Sisyphus, Camus says, also concludes that all is well. A universe without a master is, for him, neither empty nor pointless; every stone of his mountain is a world in itself. The effort of climbing, the struggle itself, is enough to fill a human heart. The essay closes with a sentence that has become one of the most quoted lines of the twentieth century: 'One must imagine Sisyphus happy.'
paras.uz: Va mashhur yakun. Sizif ham, deydi Kamyu, hammasi yaxshi degan xulosaga keladi. Xo'jayinsiz koinot uning uchun na bo'sh, na ma'nosiz; tog'ining har bir toshi o'z-o'zicha bir dunyo. Tepaga chiqish sa'y-harakati, kurashning o'zi inson yuragini to'ldirishga yetadi. Esse XX asrning eng ko'p iqtibos keltiriladigan satrlaridan biriga aylangan jumla bilan yopiladi: «Sizifni baxtli deb tasavvur qilish kerak».

chapters.title: Appendix: hope and the absurd in Kafka
chapters.title_uz: Ilova: Kafka ijodida umid va absurd

paras.en: Most editions of The Myth of Sisyphus end with an appendix on Franz Kafka. Camus wrote it for the original book, but in 1942, under German occupation, a study of a Jewish writer could not be published, so it was removed and replaced by the chapter on Kirilov. It appeared separately in 1943 and was restored to the book later. It is a fitting conclusion, because Kafka is perhaps the writer whose world looks most absurd of all — and yet Camus argues that his work, in the end, is not absurd.
paras.uz: «Sizif afsonasi»ning ko'pchilik nashrlari Frans Kafka haqidagi ilova bilan tugaydi. Kamyu uni asl kitob uchun yozgan, lekin 1942-yilda, nemis ishg'oli ostida, yahudiy yozuvchi haqidagi tadqiqotni chop etib bo'lmasdi, shuning uchun u olib tashlanib, o'rniga Kirillov haqidagi bob qo'yilgan. U 1943-yilda alohida chop etilgan va keyinroq kitobga qaytarilgan. Bu munosib yakun, chunki Kafka, ehtimol, dunyosi eng absurd ko'rinadigan yozuvchidir — shunga qaramay Kamyu uning asari oxir-oqibat absurd emasligini isbotlaydi.

paras.en: Camus begins with the experience of reading Kafka. His books, he says, force us to read them twice. The endings — or the absence of endings — suggest explanations, but never reveal them clearly. We feel that every detail could be a symbol, yet the symbols never resolve into a single meaning. The reader is drawn into the same position as Kafka's heroes: trying endlessly to interpret a world that never answers directly.
paras.uz: Kamyu Kafkani o'qish tajribasidan boshlaydi. Uning kitoblari, deydi u, bizni ularni ikki marta o'qishga majbur qiladi. Yakunlar — yoki yakunning yo'qligi — tushuntirishlarga ishora qiladi, lekin ularni hech qachon aniq ochib bermaydi. Har bir tafsilot ramz bo'lishi mumkindek tuyuladi, lekin ramzlar hech qachon bitta ma'noga birlashmaydi. O'quvchi Kafka qahramonlari bilan bir xil holatga tushadi: hech qachon to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob bermaydigan dunyoni cheksiz talqin qilishga urinadi.

paras.en: What makes Kafka's art so powerful, according to Camus, is the combination of the natural and the extraordinary. Terrible things happen in his stories, but they are told in a calm, everyday, almost bureaucratic tone. In The Trial, Joseph K. is arrested one morning without being told why. He continues to go to work, he tries to understand his case, he consults lawyers and painters and priests, and in the end he is taken out and killed — 'like a dog', as the last words of the novel say. Nobody ever explains the accusation.
paras.uz: Kamyuning fikricha, Kafka san'atini bunchalik kuchli qiladigan narsa — tabiiy va g'ayrioddiyning birikmasi. Uning hikoyalarida dahshatli voqealar sodir bo'ladi, lekin ular xotirjam, kundalik, deyarli byurokratik ohangda aytiladi. «Jarayon»da Yozef K. bir kuni ertalab sababi aytilmasdan hibsga olinadi. U ishga borishda davom etadi, ishini tushunishga urinadi, advokatlar, rassomlar va ruhoniylar bilan maslahatlashadi va oxirida olib chiqib o'ldiriladi — romanning so'nggi so'zlari aytganidek, «itdek». Hech kim ayblovni hech qachon tushuntirmaydi.

paras.en: The same is true, Camus notes, of The Metamorphosis. Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed into a huge insect, and his first worry is that he will be late for work and that his employer will be angry. This mixture — the monstrous event and the ordinary reaction — is exactly the absurd as Camus has described it: the gap between a person's habits and the inexplicable reality that suddenly breaks into his life. Kafka shows the absurd not as a theory but as a situation.
paras.uz: Kamyuning qayd etishicha, «Evrilish» haqida ham xuddi shunday. Gregor Zamza uyg'onib, o'zini ulkan hasharotga aylangan holda topadi va uning birinchi tashvishi — ishga kechikishi va xo'jayini g'azablanishi. Bu aralashma — dahshatli voqea va oddiy munosabat — Kamyu tasvirlagan absurdning aynan o'zi: insonning odatlari va uning hayotiga birdan bostirib kiradigan tushunib bo'lmaydigan haqiqat o'rtasidagi bo'shliq. Kafka absurdni nazariya sifatida emas, balki vaziyat sifatida ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: Camus illustrates this with an anecdote that has become famous. A madman is fishing in a bathtub. A doctor with modern ideas about treatment asks him, politely, whether the fish are biting. The madman answers sharply: of course not, you fool — it's a bathtub. Camus says that this story, though a joke, captures the logic of the absurd effect in Kafka: everything is perfectly reasonable inside an unreasonable situation, and the reasonable man is the one who looks foolish.
paras.uz: Kamyu buni mashhur bo'lib ketgan latifa bilan tasvirlaydi. Bir telba vannada baliq ovlayapti. Davolash haqida zamonaviy qarashlarga ega shifokor undan xushmuomalalik bilan baliq ilinyaptimi, deb so'raydi. Telba keskin javob beradi: albatta yo'q, ahmoq — bu vanna-ku. Kamyuning aytishicha, bu hikoya, hazil bo'lsa ham, Kafkadagi absurd ta'sir mantig'ini ushlaydi: aqlga sig'maydigan vaziyat ichida hamma narsa mutlaqo aqlga muvofiq va ahmoq bo'lib ko'rinadigan kishi — aqlli odam.

paras.en: Up to this point, Kafka seems to be the perfect absurd writer. But Camus looks more closely at The Castle, Kafka's last novel. Its hero, K., a land surveyor, arrives at a village dominated by a mysterious castle, and spends the whole book trying to be accepted, to be allowed in, to reach the officials who live there. He never succeeds. Camus reads the novel as a kind of theology in action: K.'s endless effort to enter the castle is the effort of a soul to reach grace.
paras.uz: Shu nuqtagacha Kafka mukammal absurd yozuvchidek ko'rinadi. Lekin Kamyu Kafkaning so'nggi romani «Qasr»ga diqqat bilan qaraydi. Uning qahramoni, yer o'lchovchi K., sirli qasr hukmron bo'lgan qishloqqa keladi va butun kitob davomida qabul qilinishga, ichkariga kiritilishga, u yerda yashaydigan amaldorlarga yetishga urinadi. U hech qachon muvaffaqiyatga erishmaydi. Kamyu romanni o'ziga xos harakatdagi ilohiyot sifatida o'qiydi: K.ning qasrga kirish uchun cheksiz sa'y-harakati — ruhning inoyatga yetish sa'y-harakati.

paras.en: This changes everything. In The Trial, Kafka diagnoses the human condition: man is accused, condemned and executed without understanding why. In The Castle, he seems to propose a treatment: in spite of everything, keep seeking; the castle exists; grace is possible, even if it is never reached. K. does not revolt against the castle — he wants to be accepted by it. The more absurd and humiliating the world becomes, the more stubbornly he hopes.
paras.uz: Bu hamma narsani o'zgartiradi. «Jarayon»da Kafka inson holatiga tashxis qo'yadi: inson nega ekanini tushunmasdan ayblanadi, hukm qilinadi va qatl etiladi. «Qasr»da u davo taklif qilayotgandek: hamma narsaga qaramay, izlashda davom et; qasr mavjud; inoyat mumkin, hatto unga hech qachon erishilmasa ham. K. qasrga qarshi isyon qilmaydi — u uning tomonidan qabul qilinishni istaydi. Dunyo qanchalik absurd va xo'rlovchi bo'lsa, u shunchalik qaysarlik bilan umid qiladi.

paras.en: Here Camus recognises the movement he described in Kierkegaard. Kafka, too, finds in the absurd itself a reason to believe. The very incomprehensibility of the castle becomes a sign that it is divine; the humiliation becomes a path. Camus is not mocking this; he finds it moving and great. But he says clearly that it is a leap. Kafka's work, which seemed to be the purest expression of the absurd, is in the end a work of hope — strange, desperate hope, but hope all the same.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Kamyu Kyerkegorda tasvirlagan harakatni taniydi. Kafka ham absurdning o'zida ishonish uchun sabab topadi. Qasrning tushunib bo'lmasligining o'zi uning ilohiy ekanining belgisiga aylanadi; xo'rlanish yo'lga aylanadi. Kamyu buni masxara qilmaydi; u buni ta'sirli va buyuk deb biladi. Lekin u bu sakrash ekanini aniq aytadi. Absurdning eng sof ifodasidek ko'ringan Kafka asari oxir-oqibat umid asari — g'alati, umidsiz umid, lekin baribir umid.

paras.en: Camus ends with a paradox. A truly absurd work, he suggests, is not universal: it stays close to one person's lucid experience and offers no message for all humanity. Kafka's work is universal precisely because it is a work of hope. It shows the face of human beings fleeing from their humanity, finding in their contradictions reasons to believe and in their despair reasons to hope. That is why so many readers, believers and non-believers alike, recognise themselves in it.
paras.uz: Kamyu paradoks bilan tugatadi. Haqiqiy absurd asar, deydi u, universal emas: u bir odamning ravshan tajribasiga yaqin qoladi va butun insoniyat uchun xabar taklif qilmaydi. Kafka asari aynan umid asari bo'lgani uchun universal. U insonlarning o'z insoniyligidan qochayotgan, ziddiyatlarida ishonish uchun va umidsizliklarida umid qilish uchun sabablar topayotgan yuzini ko'rsatadi. Shuning uchun ko'p o'quvchilar — dindorlar ham, dinsizlar ham — o'zini unda taniydi.

paras.en: With this appendix, the book closes its circle. It began with the question of suicide and the temptation of hope; it ends by showing how even the greatest artist of the absurd could not resist hope. Camus's position remains firm but respectful: he understands the leap, he admires those who made it, and he chooses not to make it himself. The absurd man, like Sisyphus, stays on the mountain — without a castle, without a judge, and still, Camus insists, able to find joy.
paras.uz: Bu ilova bilan kitob o'z doirasini yopadi. U o'z joniga qasd savoli va umid vasvasasi bilan boshlangan edi; u hatto absurdning eng buyuk san'atkori ham umidga qarshi tura olmaganini ko'rsatish bilan tugaydi. Kamyuning pozitsiyasi qat'iy, lekin hurmatli bo'lib qoladi: u sakrashni tushunadi, uni qilganlarga qoyil qoladi va o'zi uni qilmaslikni tanlaydi. Absurd inson, Sizif kabi, tog'da qoladi — qasrsiz, hakamsiz va baribir, Kamyu ta'kidlaganidek, quvonch topishga qodir.

Kamyu «Jarayon», «Qasr» va «Evrilish»ni tahlil qiladi: Kafka absurdni kundalik hayotning oddiy ohangida mukammal chizadi, lekin «Qasr»da qahramon inoyat izlaydi va Kafka ham, Kyerkegor kabi, umidga sakraydi. Xulosa: Kafka asari absurd emas, balki umid asari — va aynan shuning uchun universal.

chapters.title: After the mountain: legacy and questions

paras.en: This last chapter is not part of Camus's essay. It is WordDrop's afterword: a short review of the main ideas, a look at what happened to the book and its author, and some questions to think about. Let us begin with a summary. The absurd is the collision between the human need for meaning and a world that gives no answer. It is not found in man alone or in the world alone, but in their meeting. Faced with it, there are three temptations: to forget it through habit, to escape it through hope, or to end it through suicide.
paras.uz: Bu so'nggi bob Kamyu essesining qismi emas. Bu WordDrop so'nggi so'zi: asosiy g'oyalarning qisqa takrori, kitob va muallifining taqdiriga nazar va o'ylab ko'rish uchun savollar. Keling, xulosadan boshlaymiz. Absurd — inson ma'noga bo'lgan ehtiyoji va hech qanday javob bermaydigan dunyo o'rtasidagi to'qnashuv. U yolg'iz insonda ham, yolg'iz dunyoda ham emas, balki ularning uchrashuvida topiladi. U bilan yuzma-yuz kelganda uchta vasvasa bor: uni odat orqali unutish, undan umid orqali qochish yoki uni o'z joniga qasd orqali tugatish.

paras.en: Camus rejects all three. Instead, he proposes to keep the absurd alive, with lucidity. From it he draws three consequences: revolt, which means facing one's condition without surrender; freedom, which means being released from false hopes about tomorrow; and passion, which means living as fully and as consciously as possible. He illustrates this attitude with Don Juan, the actor, the conqueror and the creator, and he crowns it with Sisyphus, who knows his labour is endless and still, in Camus's vision, can be happy.
paras.uz: Kamyu uchalasini ham rad etadi. Buning o'rniga u absurdni ravshanlik bilan tirik saqlashni taklif qiladi. Undan u uchta oqibat chiqaradi: isyon — o'z holatiga taslim bo'lmasdan qarash; erkinlik — ertangi kun haqidagi soxta umidlardan ozod bo'lish; ehtiros — iloji boricha to'liq va ongli yashash. U bu munosabatni Don Juan, aktyor, istilochi va ijodkor bilan tasvirlaydi va uni mehnati cheksiz ekanini biladigan, shunga qaramay Kamyu nazarida baxtli bo'la oladigan Sizif bilan toj kiydiradi.

paras.en: The book appeared in October 1942, a few months after The Stranger. In 1943 Jean-Paul Sartre wrote a long and famous review of The Stranger in which he used The Myth of Sisyphus to explain it, and from then on the two books were read together. Camus and Sartre became friends and were often grouped together as 'existentialists'. Camus himself rejected that label many times. He said that his essay was written precisely against the existential philosophers, whom he accused of making the leap.
paras.uz: Kitob 1942-yil oktabrida, «Begona»dan bir necha oy keyin chiqdi. 1943-yilda Jan-Pol Sartr «Begona» haqida uzun va mashhur taqriz yozdi va unda romanni tushuntirish uchun «Sizif afsonasi»dan foydalandi; o'shandan beri ikki kitob birga o'qiladi. Kamyu va Sartr do'st bo'lishdi va ko'pincha birga «ekzistensialistlar» deb guruhlanishdi. Kamyuning o'zi bu yorliqni ko'p marta rad etgan. U o'z essesi aynan sakrash qilishda ayblagan ekzistensial faylasuflarga qarshi yozilganini aytgan.

paras.en: During the war Camus joined the French Resistance and became editor of the clandestine newspaper Combat. The experience of war and occupation pushed him beyond the solitary revolt of Sisyphus. In The Plague (1947) a whole city fights an epidemic together, and in The Rebel (1951) he develops a new formula, often summarised as 'I rebel, therefore we exist'. Revolt is no longer only one person's lucidity; it becomes the basis of solidarity with others. It also sets limits: a revolt that kills freely betrays itself.
paras.uz: Urush yillarida Kamyu fransuz Qarshilik harakatiga qo'shildi va yashirin «Combat» gazetasining muharriri bo'ldi. Urush va ishg'ol tajribasi uni Sizifning yolg'iz isyonidan nariga olib o'tdi. «Vabo» (1947) romanida butun bir shahar epidemiyaga qarshi birga kurashadi, «Isyonkor inson» (1951) kitobida esa u ko'pincha «Men isyon qilaman, demak biz mavjudmiz» deb jamlanadigan yangi formulani ishlab chiqadi. Isyon endi faqat bir odamning ravshanligi emas; u boshqalar bilan birdamlikning asosiga aylanadi. U chegaralar ham qo'yadi: bemalol o'ldiradigan isyon o'ziga xiyonat qiladi.

paras.en: The Rebel led to a painful public quarrel with Sartre in 1952, because Camus criticised revolutionary violence and the Soviet system at a time when Sartre defended it. The friendship ended. In 1957, at the age of forty-four, Camus received the Nobel Prize in Literature, one of the youngest writers ever to do so. On 4 January 1960 he was killed in a car accident in France. In his pocket, it is often told, was an unused train ticket: he had planned to travel by train and changed his mind at the last moment. Many readers have seen in this an almost absurd ending.
paras.uz: «Isyonkor inson» 1952-yilda Sartr bilan og'riqli ochiq janjalga olib keldi, chunki Kamyu Sartr inqilobiy zo'ravonlik va sovet tizimini himoya qilgan bir paytda ularni tanqid qildi. Do'stlik tugadi. 1957-yilda, qirq to'rt yoshida, Kamyu adabiyot bo'yicha Nobel mukofotini oldi — buni olgan eng yosh yozuvchilardan biri. 1960-yil 4-yanvarda u Fransiyada avtohalokatda halok bo'ldi. Ko'pincha aytilishicha, uning cho'ntagida ishlatilmagan poyezd chiptasi bo'lgan: u poyezdda borishni rejalashtirgan va so'nggi lahzada fikrini o'zgartirgan. Ko'p o'quvchilar bunda deyarli absurd yakunni ko'rgan.

paras.en: The Myth of Sisyphus has had an enormous influence, far beyond philosophy. It is read in schools and universities around the world, quoted in films, songs and novels, and the image of the happy Sisyphus has become a symbol for anyone who keeps going in a repetitive or difficult life — workers, artists, carers, students preparing for exams. Psychologists and therapists sometimes use it to talk about meaning without certainty. Its first sentence and its last sentence are among the best-known lines in modern literature.
paras.uz: «Sizif afsonasi» falsafadan ancha tashqarida ulkan ta'sir ko'rsatgan. U butun dunyo maktab va universitetlarida o'qiladi, filmlar, qo'shiqlar va romanlarda iqtibos keltiriladi, baxtli Sizif obrazi esa takroriy yoki og'ir hayotda davom etayotgan har bir kishi — ishchilar, rassomlar, parvarish qiluvchilar, imtihonga tayyorlanayotgan talabalar uchun timsolga aylangan. Psixologlar va terapevtlar ba'zan undan aniqliksiz ma'no haqida gapirish uchun foydalanadi. Uning birinchi va so'nggi jumlalari zamonaviy adabiyotdagi eng mashhur satrlar qatorida.

paras.en: The book also has serious critics, and an honest reader should know their arguments. Some philosophers say that Camus's logic is weak: why should the absurd require us to 'keep' it at all, rather than simply accept it calmly? Others think his ethics of quantity is dangerous, because if no experience is better than another, cruelty could be justified as just another experience. Camus himself saw this danger: his play Caligula shows an emperor who takes the absurd as permission to kill, and the play is a warning, not a model.
paras.uz: Kitobning jiddiy tanqidchilari ham bor va halol o'quvchi ularning dalillarini bilishi kerak. Ba'zi faylasuflar Kamyu mantig'i zaif deydi: nega absurd uni xotirjam qabul qilish o'rniga, uni «saqlab qolishni» talab qilishi kerak? Boshqalar uning miqdor axloqi xavfli deb hisoblaydi, chunki agar hech bir tajriba boshqasidan yaxshiroq bo'lmasa, shafqatsizlikni yana bir tajriba sifatida oqlash mumkin. Kamyuning o'zi bu xavfni ko'rgan: uning «Kaligula» pyesasi absurdni o'ldirishga ruxsat deb qabul qilgan imperatorni ko'rsatadi va pyesa namuna emas, balki ogohlantirishdir.

paras.en: Religious thinkers, for their part, argue that Camus's rejection of hope is itself a choice that goes beyond evidence: if we cannot know that there is a meaning, we also cannot know that there is none, so faith is not necessarily dishonest. Others ask whether the happiness of Sisyphus is real or only a brave pose. And some readers from less privileged backgrounds ask whether it is fair to tell people trapped in exhausting work that they should imagine themselves happy. These are good questions, and Camus's later books show that he took some of them seriously.
paras.uz: Diniy mutafakkirlar esa o'z navbatida Kamyuning umidni rad etishi o'zi ham dalillardan oshib ketadigan tanlov, deb ta'kidlaydi: agar biz ma'no borligini bila olmasak, uning yo'qligini ham bila olmaymiz, demak iymon albatta insofsizlik emas. Boshqalar Sizifning baxti haqiqiymi yoki faqat jasur qiyofami, deb so'raydi. Ba'zi o'quvchilar esa charchatuvchi mehnatga qamalib qolgan odamlarga o'zlarini baxtli deb tasavvur qilishni aytish adolatlimi, deb so'raydi. Bular yaxshi savollar va Kamyuning keyingi kitoblari u ulardan ba'zilarini jiddiy qabul qilganini ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: Here are some questions to think about or discuss. Do you agree that suicide is the 'one serious question' of philosophy, or is that an exaggeration? Have you ever experienced the moment when routine suddenly asks 'why?' What do you think of Camus's distinction between the absurd and despair? Is hope always an escape, or can it be honest? Which of the absurd figures — Don Juan, the actor, the conqueror, the creator — seems most convincing to you, and which seems most dangerous?
paras.uz: Mana o'ylab ko'rish yoki muhokama qilish uchun bir nechta savol. Siz o'z joniga qasd falsafaning «yagona jiddiy savoli» ekaniga qo'shilasizmi yoki bu mubolag'ami? Siz hech qachon kundalik tartib birdan «nega?» deb so'raydigan lahzani boshdan kechirganmisiz? Kamyuning absurd va umidsizlik o'rtasidagi farqi haqida nima deb o'ylaysiz? Umid har doim qochishmi yoki u halol bo'lishi mumkinmi? Absurd qiyofalardan qaysi biri — Don Juan, aktyor, istilochi, ijodkor — sizga eng ishonarli, qaysi biri eng xavfli ko'rinadi?

paras.en: And finally: what is your rock? Everyone carries something that must be pushed up the hill again tomorrow — work, study, illness, care for others, a language that still feels difficult. Camus does not promise that the rock will stay at the top. He suggests something else: that the effort itself, lived with open eyes, can be enough to fill a heart. Learning English, too, has something of Sisyphus in it: the words roll back, and we push them up again. Perhaps, in those moments, we can imagine ourselves happy.
paras.uz: Va nihoyat: sizning toshingiz nima? Har kim ertaga yana tepaga itarib chiqarilishi kerak bo'lgan nimanidir ko'taradi — ish, o'qish, kasallik, boshqalarga g'amxo'rlik, hali ham qiyin tuyuladigan til. Kamyu tosh cho'qqida qolishini va'da qilmaydi. U boshqa narsani taklif qiladi: ko'zlar ochiq holda yashalgan sa'y-harakatning o'zi yurakni to'ldirishga yetishi mumkin. Ingliz tilini o'rganishda ham Sizifdan nimadir bor: so'zlar dumalab ketadi va biz ularni yana tepaga itaramiz. Balki o'sha lahzalarda o'zimizni baxtli deb tasavvur qila olarmiz.

quiz.q: How did Camus react to being called an 'existentialist'?
o: He rejected the label many times
quiz.why_uz: U essesi aynan ekzistensial faylasuflarga qarshi yozilganini aytgan.

quiz.q: What new idea of revolt appears in The Rebel?
o: Revolt as the basis of solidarity: 'I rebel, therefore we exist'
quiz.why_uz: Isyon endi boshqalar bilan birdamlik asosiga aylanadi.

quiz.q: Which play by Camus shows the danger of taking the absurd as permission to kill?
quiz.why_uz: «Kaligula» — ogohlantirish, namuna emas.
